defects.quote: reinforced by extensive GWAS catalog mappings (114 unique SNPs, including the well-known rs738409 variant)
defects.why_wrong: rs738409 appears nowhere in this run's ledger. get_gwas_catalog returned n_unique_snps=114 and exactly six example_rsids: rs4823182, rs11912828, rs2073080, rs8418, rs2179642, rs3788603. The model supplied the famous PNPLA3 I148M variant from memory and dressed it as a GWAS Catalog return. It is the correct variant biologically, which is exactly why no human reviewer will stop on it — and the tool never named it. For this to be earned, get_gwas_catalog would have had to return rs738409 in its rsID list (or a per-SNP association row for MASLD).
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The fabricated-rsID check evidently only rejects rsIDs that fail a plausibility/format test or that contradict a complete list; here the tool returned an explicitly partial sample (6 of 114), so an unlisted-but-real rsID passes. Validator ran checked:7 and flagged only the 'small-molecule' token.
defects.suggested_fix: Delete 'including the well-known rs738409 variant'. If a specific variant is wanted, the ledger must carry it: extend get_gwas_catalog to return the trait-matched association rows, and have the validator treat example_rsids as a closed set unless sweep_complete plus a full rsID list is present.

defects.quote: GO — Strong genetic and biological evidence supports TREM2 as a causal target for Alzheimer disease, through microglial activation and amyloid-beta clearance.
defects.why_wrong: No tool in this run mentions microglia, amyloid-beta, or clearance. The complete UniProt return is a protein name ('Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2'), subcellular locations, and a disease list; get_target_disease_evidence returns only numeric datatype scores. The entire mechanistic clause is recited neurobiology. For it to be earned, get_uniprot_dossier would have had to return a function/GO annotation stating microglial activation and amyloid-beta binding — the dossier has no function field at all.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'microglial activation' and 'amyloid-beta clearance' are not on the fixed qualitative-claim list (monoclonal antibody, FDA-approved, small-molecule, clinical trial, gene therapy, pathogenic variant), contain no numbers, no rsIDs and no accessions, so there is nothing for a regex to compare against the ledger.
defects.suggested_fix: Cut the mechanism clause from the verdict, or add a function/GO-term field to get_uniprot_dossier and restrict mechanism sentences to strings that appear verbatim in that field.

defects.quote: is explicitly annotated in UniProt as playing a causal role in Alzheimer disease 17 via amyloid-beta and lipoprotein binding
defects.why_wrong: The word 'explicitly' makes this a direct claim about what the tool returned, and it is false. get_uniprot_dossier returned diseases: ['Polycystic lipomembranous osteodysplasia with sclerosing leukoencephalopathy 2', 'Alzheimer disease 17'] — a bare disease-association list, with no causal language and no binding-partner information. 'via amyloid-beta and lipoprotein binding' paraphrases the real UniProt entry the model memorised, not the JSON this pipeline captured. Worse, a disease listed in a UniProt dossier is an association, not an attribution of causality.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'Alzheimer disease 17' is a genuine string in the ledger, so any token-overlap heuristic sees a supported sentence; the fabricated part is the appended mechanism, which has no numeric or ID handle for the regex.
defects.suggested_fix: Rewrite as 'UniProt lists Alzheimer disease 17 among TREM2 disease annotations' and drop the binding mechanism. Add a validator rule that any sentence beginning 'annotated in UniProt as...' must quote only fields actually present in the dossier payload.

defects.quote: ClinVar records contain established pathogenic variants in TREM2 linked to neurodegenerative phenotypes
defects.why_wrong: get_clinvar_variants returns only total_records=202, pathogenic_in_sample=5, sample_size=30 — counts, with no variant identities and no phenotype/condition field whatsoever. 'linked to neurodegenerative phenotypes' is Nasu-Hakola/AD knowledge supplied by the model. The tool also warns the count is a 30-record sample, so 'established' overstates even the part that exists.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'pathogenic variant' is on the qualitative list and get_clinvar_variants did report pathogenic_in_sample>0, so the token check is satisfied; the unsupported half of the sentence is the phenotype linkage, which the ledger has no field for and the regex therefore cannot test.
defects.suggested_fix: Restate as 'ClinVar reports 5 pathogenic records among 30 sampled of 202 total for TREM2; conditions were not retrieved.' Have get_clinvar_variants return the condition names if phenotype claims are to be permitted at all.

defects.quote: GO — VKORC1 is a well-established, clinically validated target whose inhibition by coumarin anticoagulants is directly used for the prevention and treatment of venous thrombosis.
defects.why_wrong: Nothing in this run states a therapeutic indication. get_pharmgkb_drug_gene returned drug names (acenocoumarol, fluindione, phenprocoumon, warfarin) attached to genotype-response annotations — that is pharmacogenomics, not an indication. get_chembl_modulators returned seven anonymous CHEMBL IDs with action INHIBITOR and no approval, phase, or indication field. 'Anticoagulant' as a drug class, and 'used for the prevention and treatment of venous thrombosis', are pure pretrained clinical knowledge. To be earned, a tool would have had to return an indication or label field (none of the eight does). Note also that the same card's Open Targets return gives genetic_association 0.0312 — near zero — while the reasoning closes on 'the wealth of clinical and genetic validation'.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The model avoided the flagged tokens: it wrote 'clinically validated' and 'directly used for' instead of 'FDA-approved' or 'clinical trial'. Every drug name it cites is genuinely in the ledger, so name-matching passes; only the claimed purpose of those drugs is invented, and no field exists to compare it against.
defects.suggested_fix: Replace with 'PharmGKB links VKORC1 variation to four coumarin drugs (38 annotations, 3 at level 1A); no tool in this run returned an approved indication.' Extend the qualitative-claim list from a token blacklist to a claim-type check: any indication/approval/usage assertion requires a ledger field that carries indications.

defects.quote: PharmGKB demonstrates extensive pharmacogenomic annotations linking VKORC1 variation to coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin and acenocoumarol) for dosing and toxicity outcomes
defects.why_wrong: 'for dosing and toxicity outcomes' names PharmGKB annotation categories that this run never retrieved. get_pharmgkb_drug_gene returned only n_clinical_annotations=38, evidence_level_counts, a drug list and n_drugs — no phenotype category, no annotation text. The model knows warfarin PGx is about dose and bleeding risk and filled the gap. For this to be earned, the tool would have had to return the annotation phenotype-category field ('Dosage', 'Toxicity').
defects.why_validator_missed_it: Drug names and the general shape of the sentence match the ledger; 'dosing' and 'toxicity' are unremarkable English words on no blacklist and map to no number, rsID or accession.
defects.suggested_fix: Truncate at the drug list, or add phenotype_categories to the PharmGKB tool return and permit the clause only when those strings are present.

defects.quote: Furthermore, PCSK9 has 246 GWAS associations and is successfully targeted therapeutically by RNAi and biologic modulators in clinical practice.
defects.why_wrong: Two leaks in one clause. (1) 'biologic modulators': get_chembl_modulators resolved to target 'PCSK9 mRNA' (CHEMBL4630662) and returned exactly two entries, both RNAI INHIBITOR. An mRNA target cannot host an antibody, and no antibody, protein or 'biologic' appears anywhere in the ledger — the model is remembering evolocumab/alirocumab. (2) 'successfully ... in clinical practice': no tool returns approval, usage or outcome data, and this card's get_pharmgkb_drug_gene came back found:false, i.e. this run has zero clinical-pharmacology evidence for PCSK9. Open Targets clinical=0.9704 is an evidence-type score, not a statement that therapy works in practice.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'biologic' is not the blacklisted token 'monoclonal antibody', and ChEMBL returned found:true with modulators, so a modality claim keyed to 'are there modulators?' passes. 'in clinical practice' evades both 'FDA-approved' and 'clinical trial'. The one number, 246, matches n_association_rows so the numeric check is satisfied and the card scores checked:1, ok:true.
defects.suggested_fix: Rewrite as 'ChEMBL lists two RNAi inhibitors against PCSK9 mRNA; no other modality and no approval status was retrieved, and PharmGKB returned no annotations.' Validator: derive allowed modality words from the ChEMBL action/moa strings actually returned and reject any modality noun not present there.

defects.quote: Furthermore, IL6R is well-druggable with known modulators and clinically approved receptor inhibitors (such as tocilizumab) already documented in PharmGKB.
defects.why_wrong: 'clinically approved' is nowhere in the ledger. get_pharmgkb_drug_gene returned drugs:['tocilizumab'] with n_clinical_annotations=3 at evidence levels 3 and 4 — the two weakest tiers — which says a genotype-drug-response association has been reported, not that the drug is approved. get_chembl_modulators returned four anonymous CHEMBL IDs with no approval or max-phase field. The drug name is legitimately in the ledger; its regulatory status is imported memory, and calling it a 'receptor inhibitor' also imports a mechanism PharmGKB never states.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The blacklist contains 'FDA-approved'; the model wrote 'clinically approved', a synonym the regex does not cover. 'tocilizumab' string-matches the PharmGKB payload, so the sentence looks anchored. Card scored ok:true, checked:4.
defects.suggested_fix: Rewrite as 'PharmGKB records 3 clinical annotations (levels 3-4) linking IL6R to tocilizumab; approval status was not retrieved by any tool.' Broaden the approval regex to /\b(FDA[- ]approved|clinically approved|approved|licensed|marketed|on the market)\b/ and require an explicit approval field to satisfy it.

defects.quote: GO — genetic and Mendelian randomization evidence supports a causal, protective role of IL6R inhibition in coronary heart disease.
defects.why_wrong: The retrieved estimate is beta = -0.0442 for the IL6R protein exposure on coronary heart disease (rs4129267, cis, Wald ratio). Taken as the ledger presents it — exposure is plasma protein level — a negative beta means HIGHER IL6R protein goes with LOWER CHD, which on its face argues that inhibition would be harmful, not protective. The card's conclusion is nonetheless the biologically correct one, because the Asp358Ala instrument raises soluble IL6R while damping classic IL-6 signalling — a sIL6R paradox the model knows from the tocilizumab/CHD literature. That inversion is supplied entirely from pretraining: nothing in get_mr_result labels the exposure, states its direction of effect on signalling, or licenses reading a negative protein-level beta as 'inhibition is protective'. This is the most dangerous shape of leakage — a reviewer who checks the sign against the text sees a contradiction, and a reviewer who knows the biology waves it through, while the pipeline established neither.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The MR tool returned found:true with a real estimate, so the causal-language gate opens; -0.044 is quoted accurately elsewhere in the reasoning so the numeric check passes. The validator has no model of what the exposure is or which direction of intervention a sign implies, so a sign flip between the number and the recommendation is invisible to it. Card scored ok:true.
defects.suggested_fix: Make get_mr_result state the exposure explicitly ('exposure = plasma IL6R level, 1 SD increase') and have the renderer emit the mechanical reading ('higher IL6R -> lower CHD risk'). Require any 'inhibition is protective/harmful' sentence to agree with that mechanical reading, or to cite a ledger field that documents the instrument's signalling direction. Until then the verdict should read 'higher genetically proxied IL6R levels associate with lower CHD risk; the therapeutic direction is not established by this evidence.'

defects.quote: GO — Robust genetic and causal evidence demonstrates that elevated LPA levels strongly increase coronary heart disease risk, supported by clinical-stage antisense and RNAi inhibitors.
defects.why_wrong: 'clinical-stage' is not in the ledger, and it recurs in the reasoning as 'ChEMBL identifies active clinical modulators'. get_chembl_modulators returned two entries against target 'LPA mRNA' with actions RNAI INHIBITOR and ANTISENSE INHIBITOR and no phase, status, or development-stage field of any kind. The model knows pelacarsen and olpasiran are in late-phase trials and promoted two bare ChEMBL IDs to clinical assets. For 'clinical-stage' to be earned, get_chembl_modulators would have had to return max_phase or a development-status field.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The blacklisted phrase is 'clinical trial'; 'clinical-stage' and 'active clinical modulators' are near-synonyms the regex does not match, and ChEMBL found:true with two modulators, so the existence half of the claim checks out. Card scored ok:true.
defects.suggested_fix: Say 'ChEMBL lists two nucleic-acid inhibitors against LPA mRNA; development stage was not retrieved.' Add max_phase to the ChEMBL return and gate every stage/approval word on it.

defects.quote: Although gnomAD constraint metrics indicate loss-of-function intolerance and the EpiGraphDB pQTL resource has no available MR estimate, the extensive clinical legacy of HMGCR inhibition provides definitive proof of efficacy.
defects.why_wrong: 'Definitive proof of efficacy' rests on statin outcome trials the model remembers; this run retrieved no efficacy data at all. The eight tools return association scores, constraint metrics, counts, accessions and drug names — none returns a trial result or an outcome. Open Targets clinical=0.9984 means clinical-type evidence is abundant for that ontology term, not that inhibition works. The sentence is doing real damage here because it is deployed specifically to overrule two caveats the ledger raised: gnomAD's 'LoF-INTOLERANT ... inhibiting it carries a safety warning' and the MR tool's 'ABSENCE OF AN ESTIMATE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF NO EFFECT'. Remembered efficacy is used to dismiss a declared safety flag.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: It carries no number, no ID, and none of the blacklisted qualitative tokens. The validator did fire on this card, but only for the word 'causal' in the verdict; 'definitive proof of efficacy' passed untouched because efficacy is not a claim class the checker models.
defects.suggested_fix: Delete the clause. The honest close is 'no MR estimate is available for this pair and gnomAD flags HMGCR as LoF-intolerant; efficacy evidence was not retrieved by any tool in this run.' Add an efficacy/outcome claim class to the validator that no current tool can satisfy, so such sentences are always rejected.

defects.quote: ChEMBL lists multiple small-molecule inhibitors targeting this enzyme.
defects.why_wrong: get_chembl_modulators returned six listed entries (n_modulators=10) as bare CHEMBL IDs with action INHIBITOR and moa 'HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor'. There is no modality field; 'small-molecule' comes from the model knowing statins are small molecules. Same defect class as the PCSK9 'biologic' leak, and the same fix applies.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'small-molecule' IS on the blacklist and was flagged on PNPLA3 and TREM2 — but only because ChEMBL returned no modulators there. The rule is evidently 'modality claim OK if any modulator exists', which is the wrong test: existence of a modulator says nothing about its modality. This card passed the token check.
defects.suggested_fix: Change the small-molecule rule from 'modulators exist' to 'a returned moa/action string names that modality', and add molecule_type to the ChEMBL return.

defects.quote: UniProt confirms its primary function in voltage-dependent sodium permeability in excitable membranes and its direct link to epileptic encephalopathy and seizure disorders.
defects.why_wrong: 'UniProt confirms' is a direct claim about the tool return, and the return contains no function annotation: get_uniprot_dossier gave accession Q99250, protein_name 'Sodium channel protein type 2 subunit alpha', subcellular_location ['Cell membrane'], and a three-item disease list. 'Voltage-dependent sodium ion permeability of excitable membranes' is near-verbatim the real UniProt function line — which is precisely the tell: the model is quoting a database entry it memorised rather than the payload this run captured. The disease half of the sentence is legitimate (the dossier does list 'Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 11' and 'Seizures, benign familial infantile, 3'), which camouflages the fabricated half.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: Half the sentence string-matches the disease list, the protein name plausibly implies a sodium channel, and there is no number or accession to test. The card scored checked:0, ok:true — nothing in it was checkable at all.
defects.suggested_fix: Either add a function/CC-FUNCTION field to get_uniprot_dossier and require function sentences to quote it, or restrict UniProt-attributed sentences to the fields actually in the payload: name, locations, diseases, accession.

defects.quote: GO — genetic and Mendelian randomization evidence supports a causal, protective role of IL6R inhibition in coronary heart disease.
defects.why_wrong: The retrieved estimate is a pQTL MR: exposure = plasma IL6R protein level, outcome = CHD, beta = -0.0442. Read off the ledger, the negative sign means HIGHER measured IL6R protein maps to LOWER CHD risk. The card inverts this into 'IL6R inhibition' being protective. The reconciliation that actually makes the card's sentence true (rs4129267/Asp358Ala raises soluble IL6R while blunting classic IL-6 signalling, so blockade mimics the protective allele) is pure outside knowledge — nothing in get_mr_result, get_uniprot_dossier or get_chembl_modulators states what the pQTL exposure means mechanistically or that lowering the protein reproduces the sign. As written, the ledger's sign points the opposite way to the recommendation.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: beta = -0.044 is reproduced verbatim and matches the ledger numerically, so the number check passes; MR was found=true so the causal-language rule is satisfied. The validator has no model of what the exposure is or of which direction of perturbation the sign implies.
defects.suggested_fix: State the estimate in its own terms and stop: 'higher genetically-proxied plasma IL6R associates with lower CHD (beta = -0.044, p = 2.2e-07, single cis SNP rs4129267)'. Do not translate a protein-level beta into a direction of pharmacological modulation unless a tool in the ledger establishes that mapping.

defects.quote: clinically approved receptor inhibitors (such as tocilizumab) already documented in PharmGKB
defects.why_wrong: PharmGKB returned only: n_clinical_annotations 3, evidence levels {3: 2, 4: 1}, drugs ['tocilizumab']. It says nothing about regulatory approval, and PharmGKB clinical annotations are variant-drug-response records (levels 3/4 = the weakest tiers), not indication or approval records. Worse for this card, whatever indication those annotations concern, it is not coronary heart disease — they are being imported into a CHD GO case. 'Clinically approved' is knowledge the model brought with it.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The fixed qualitative-claim list contains 'FDA-approved'; 'clinically approved' is a different string and slips past the regex. The drug name tocilizumab does appear in the ledger, so the name check passes and the approval predicate rides along with it.
defects.suggested_fix: Reduce to what the tools returned: 'ChEMBL lists 4 modulators (3 inhibitors, 1 antagonist) against the IL-6 receptor alpha subunit; PharmGKB holds 3 low-level (3/4) clinical annotations for tocilizumab, none of which concern coronary heart disease.' Drop approval status entirely.

defects.quote: Retrieved published Mendelian randomization estimates suggest a significant protective effect of genetically proxied IL6R modulation on coronary heart disease (beta = -0.044, p = 2.2e-07).
defects.why_wrong: get_mr_result attached an explicit instruction: 'Check cis_or_trans, steiger_direction_ok, and coloc_prob before treating this as causal; coloc_prob=null means colocalization was not available for this pair.' For this row steiger_direction_ok = 'NA', steiger_p = null, coloc_prob = null, heterogeneity_q_p = null, ld_check = null, n_snp = 1. Every check the tool named as a precondition for a causal reading is unavailable, yet the card asserts causality and the verdict leads with it. Contrast the LPA card, where steiger_direction_ok = 'TRUE' and ld_check = 1.0 — the ledger distinguishes these two rows and the reasoning does not.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The validator's causal-language rule is binary on MR found/not-found. found=true, so any amount of causal language is permitted regardless of the quality fields inside the record.
defects.suggested_fix: Carry the tool's own qualifiers into the text: 'single-SNP Wald ratio on a cis instrument; Steiger direction check unavailable (NA) and no colocalization probability, so directionality and shared-signal cannot be confirmed from this record.'

defects.quote: is successfully targeted therapeutically by RNAi and biologic modulators in clinical practice
defects.why_wrong: get_chembl_modulators resolved to target 'PCSK9 mRNA' (CHEMBL4630662) and returned exactly two entries, both action 'RNAI INHIBITOR'. There is no biologic, no antibody and no protein-level target in this run's ledger at all — an mRNA target cannot host a biologic modulator. 'In clinical practice' likewise appears in no tool output. Both halves of the phrase are the model recalling evolocumab/alirocumab/inclisiran from training. The card also ignores the tool's own note asking to 'confirm this is the intended target' for the mRNA resolution.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'monoclonal antibody' is on the fixed qualitative-claim list; 'biologic' is not, and 'in clinical practice' evades the 'FDA-approved'/'clinical trial' tokens. No number or accession is fabricated, so every other check passes.
defects.suggested_fix: 'ChEMBL (target resolved to PCSK9 mRNA, not the protein) lists 2 RNAi inhibitors; no protein-level modulator record was retrieved in this run.' Remove 'biologic' and 'in clinical practice'.

defects.quote: PCSK9 has 246 GWAS associations
defects.why_wrong: 246 is get_gwas_catalog's n_association_rows — a gene-level sweep across every trait in the GWAS Catalog, with no trait field returned anywhere in the record (only 107 unique SNPs and six example rsIDs). The sentence sits inside a paragraph arguing the PCSK9–hypercholesterolemia case, so a trait-agnostic row count is presented as disease-specific genetic support. The run never established that any of the 246 rows concerns cholesterol. It also silently swaps the association-row count for the SNP count, inflating 107 SNPs into '246 associations'.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 246 is present verbatim in the ledger, so the numeric comparison passes. The validator matches values, not the semantics of the field the value came from, and cannot tell that the count is unstratified by trait.
defects.suggested_fix: 'The GWAS Catalog sweep returns 246 association rows over 107 unique SNPs mapped to PCSK9 across all traits; this endpoint does not return trait labels, so none of these can be attributed to hypercholesterolemia in this run.'

defects.quote: the extensive clinical legacy of HMGCR inhibition provides definitive proof of efficacy
defects.why_wrong: No tool in this run reports a trial, an outcome, an approval or an efficacy result. The Open Targets clinical datatype score (0.9984) is an aggregated evidence score for the HMGCR–HP_0003124 pair, not a demonstration of efficacy, and PharmGKB returned only ten level-3 annotations. 'Extensive clinical legacy' and 'definitive proof of efficacy' are recalled facts about statins. The sentence is also used to overrule a caveat the ledger declared: get_gnomad_constraint returned pLI 0.9999, LOEUF 0.43 and the verdict 'LoF-INTOLERANT ... inhibiting it carries a safety warning', which the card acknowledges and then dismisses with unretrieved evidence.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The phrase contains no number, no accession, and none of the fixed tokens ('FDA-approved', 'clinical trial'); the validator's only complaint on this card was the word 'causal'. Prose that asserts a body of evidence without naming a specific fact is invisible to a token-matching checker.
defects.suggested_fix: Delete the clause. If a clinical statement is wanted, bound it to the ledger: 'Open Targets assigns a clinical-evidence datatype score of 0.9984 for this target-disease pair,' and leave the gnomAD LoF-intolerance warning standing rather than overriding it.

defects.quote: strong pharmacogenomic annotations with statins in PharmGKB
defects.why_wrong: get_pharmgkb_drug_gene returned evidence_level_counts {'3': 10} — all ten annotations are PharmGKB level 3, the tier meaning a single study or limited/conflicting replication. Calling them 'strong' inverts the field's meaning. Compare the VKORC1 card in the same bundle, where levels 1A/1B/2A are actually present: the ledger clearly distinguishes strength tiers and this card ignores the tier it got. Separately, PharmGKB annotations describe variant-drug RESPONSE (statin efficacy/myopathy in treated patients); they are being used here as reinforcement of a target-disease association, which is a different question.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: No number is quoted, so nothing is compared; 'strong' is an adjective, and the validator has no notion of an evidence-level ordinal or of what a pharmacogenomic annotation is evidence FOR.
defects.suggested_fix: 'PharmGKB holds 10 clinical annotations for HMGCR, all at evidence level 3 (lowest tier), covering statin response — pharmacogenetic dose/response evidence, not target-disease validation.'

defects.quote: reinforced by numerous GWAS Catalog associations
defects.why_wrong: get_gwas_catalog returned 92 unique SNPs / 177 association rows mapped to the HMGCR locus across all traits, with no trait labels exposed. Presenting them as reinforcement of the hypercholesterolemia association attributes a trait-blind gene-level sweep to one specific disease. Nothing in the run links any of those rows to cholesterol.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'Numerous' is unquantified, so there is no number to check against the ledger, and the validator cannot see that the underlying count is unstratified by trait.
defects.suggested_fix: Either state the count with its scope ('177 association rows across all traits at this locus; traits not returned by this endpoint') or drop the clause from the disease-specific argument.

defects.quote: is explicitly annotated in UniProt as playing a causal role in Alzheimer disease 17 via amyloid-beta and lipoprotein binding
defects.why_wrong: get_uniprot_dossier returned exactly four content fields: protein_name, accession, subcellular_location ['Cell membrane','Secreted','Secreted'] and diseases ['Polycystic lipomembranous osteodysplasia with sclerosing leukoencephalopathy 2','Alzheimer disease 17']. A disease-name string in a list is not an annotation of a 'causal role', and the words amyloid-beta, lipoprotein and binding appear nowhere in any tool return in this card. A specific mechanism is attributed, by name, to a tool that returned no function field — the most damaging form of misattribution because a reader can see the tool name and assume it was checked.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'Alzheimer disease 17' is a real ledger string, so the phrase is anchored to something checkable; the mechanism words are free text with no number, accession or listed token. The validator does not verify that a claim attributed to tool X corresponds to a field tool X actually returned.
defects.suggested_fix: 'UniProt lists TREM2 (Q9NZC2) under two disease entries, one of which is Alzheimer disease 17; this dossier returns no functional annotation, so no mechanism can be sourced from it in this run.'

defects.quote: through microglial activation and amyloid-beta clearance
defects.why_wrong: The word microglia appears in no tool result for this card, nor does any pathway, cell type or clearance mechanism. This is textbook TREM2 biology carried in from training and placed in the VERDICT line — the single sentence a reader most likely acts on. It also silently supplies the direction of intended intervention (activation, i.e. agonism), which nothing in the ledger supports; ChEMBL returned n_modulators = 0 and no MR estimate matched Alzheimer disease.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: It is a mechanism phrase with no numbers, rsIDs, accessions or listed qualitative tokens, and it is factually correct biology — precisely the class the validator has no handle on.
defects.suggested_fix: Cut the mechanism clause from the verdict. The verdict should not name a mode of action (activation vs inhibition) that no retrieved tool supports.

defects.quote: ClinVar records contain established pathogenic variants in TREM2 linked to neurodegenerative phenotypes
defects.why_wrong: get_clinvar_variants returned total_records 202, pathogenic_in_sample 5, sample_size 30 — a count only. It returns no variant identifiers, no phenotypes and no condition names, and it explicitly warns the count is over a 30-record sample. 'Linked to neurodegenerative phenotypes' adds a phenotype annotation the tool never produced, and 'established' upgrades a 5-of-30 sample into a curated body of variants.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'Pathogenic variant' is on the fixed qualitative-claim list and the ledger does contain pathogenic_in_sample = 5, so the token check is satisfied. The phenotype attribution is a separate assertion the checker never tests.
defects.suggested_fix: 'ClinVar holds 202 records for TREM2; 5 of the 30 records sampled in this run are classified pathogenic. Phenotype/condition labels were not retrieved, so no link to a neurodegenerative phenotype can be made from this call.'

defects.quote: UniProt confirms its primary function in voltage-dependent sodium permeability in excitable membranes
defects.why_wrong: get_uniprot_dossier for SCN2A returned protein_name 'Sodium channel protein type 2 subunit alpha', subcellular_location ['Cell membrane'] and three disease names. There is no function field in the return. The quoted phrase is near-verbatim UniProt function text reproduced from training — correct, unverifiable from this run, and falsely credited to a tool call whose output a reader could check and would not find it in. Only the disease half of the sentence ('epileptic encephalopathy and seizure disorders') is actually in the ledger.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The sentence carries no number, rsID or accession, and 'voltage-dependent sodium permeability' is on no token list. The validator does not test whether an attributed field exists in the named tool's return.
defects.suggested_fix: 'UniProt identifies SCN2A (Q99250) as sodium channel protein type 2 subunit alpha, cell-membrane localised, with disease entries for benign familial infantile seizures 3, developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 11, and episodic ataxia 9. No functional description was returned by this call.'

defects.quote: ClinVar lists thousands of records for the gene, including numerous pathogenic variants
defects.why_wrong: The tool returned total_records 3108 and pathogenic_in_sample 11 with sample_size 30, plus the explicit warning: 'Pathogenic count is over the 30 record(s) retrieved, NOT over all 3108 ClinVar records for this gene; it is a sample, not a rate.' The sentence welds the 3108 total to the sampled pathogenic count so that 'thousands of records, including numerous pathogenic variants' reads as thousands of records of which many are pathogenic. Eleven of thirty sampled records is the only fact retrieved, and it licenses no statement about the other 3078. The verdict repeats the inflation as 'extensive clinical variant data'.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: Neither 3108 nor 11 is quoted, so there is nothing to compare numerically; 'thousands' and 'numerous' are vague quantifiers that a value-matching regex cannot evaluate, and the sampling caveat lives in a tool note the checker does not reconcile against prose.
defects.suggested_fix: 'ClinVar holds 3108 records for SCN2A; of the 30 records sampled in this run, 11 are classified pathogenic — a sample, not a rate over the full record set.'

defects.quote: the overwhelming genetic and clinical validation establishes it as a prime target for epilepsy
defects.why_wrong: Everything retrieved (Open Targets 0.9057, UniProt disease entries, ClinVar counts) establishes that SCN2A variation is ASSOCIATED with epilepsy — it says nothing about which direction of modulation would help. Against that, get_gnomad_constraint returned pLI = 1, LOEUF = 0.154, lof_z = 10.4 with the declared caveat 'inhibiting it carries a safety warning', and get_chembl_modulators returned n_modulators = 0 for the resolved target SCN2A/SCN1B. The card acknowledges the constraint caveat in a subordinate clause and then overrides it with the association evidence, which is not evidence about the same question. A GO on a target with zero retrieved modulators and the strongest LoF-intolerance signal in the bundle does not follow from the assembled ledger.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: MR returned found=false and the card avoids the word 'causal', so the causal-language rule is not triggered; nothing numeric is misquoted. Whether a verdict follows from the evidence set is outside a regex checker's reach.
defects.suggested_fix: Downgrade to REVIEW/CAUTION and state the conflict: strong disease association, but LoF-intolerance (pLI 1, LOEUF 0.15) argues against an inhibitory strategy and no ChEMBL modulator was retrieved; the retrieved evidence does not indicate which direction of modulation is therapeutic.

defects.quote: including the well-known rs738409 variant
defects.why_wrong: get_gwas_catalog returned six example rsIDs for PNPLA3 — rs4823182, rs11912828, rs2073080, rs8418, rs2179642, rs3788603 — and rs738409 is not among them, nor does it appear anywhere else in this card's ledger. The model supplied the famous I148M variant from memory and presented it as retrieved. It is the single most load-bearing genetic fact in the paragraph, it is correct, and this run never touched it.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The rsID check can only compare against the six example_rsids exposed out of 114 unique SNPs; because the list is explicitly truncated, an unlisted-but-plausible rsID cannot be disproved and is let through. A leaked identifier that happens to be real hides inside exactly that gap.
defects.suggested_fix: Name only rsIDs present in the ledger, or say 'the sweep returns 114 unique SNPs; individual rsIDs beyond the six examples returned were not retrieved in this run.'

defects.quote: While ChEMBL currently lists no small-molecule modulators
defects.why_wrong: get_chembl_modulators returned found=false with note 'No ChEMBL target for PNPLA3.' — the lookup did not resolve a target at all, so no modulator query was ever run. That is a failed resolution, not a curated finding of zero modulators. Compare OR51E2 and TREM2 in this bundle, where a target DID resolve and n_modulators = 0 was genuinely returned; the ledger distinguishes those two situations and the card collapses them. The card also asserts the absent modulators are specifically 'small-molecule', a modality the tool never had a chance to report.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The validator caught the 'small-molecule' token but has no rule for found=false semantics — it cannot tell a resolution failure from a legitimate empty result set, so the negative framing passes.
defects.suggested_fix: 'ChEMBL returned no target record for PNPLA3 in this run (lookup did not resolve), so the modulator landscape is unknown rather than empty.'

defects.quote: UniProt confirms its primary role in lipid droplet metabolism
defects.why_wrong: The only supporting content in get_uniprot_dossier is subcellular_location ['Membrane','Lipid droplet'] — a localisation field. Where a protein sits is not what it does; 'primary role in lipid droplet metabolism' converts a location annotation into a functional claim, and 'confirms' implies the dossier asserted a role it never stated. The protein_name ('1-acylglycerol-3-phosphate O-acyltransferase PNPLA3') is the only functional hint returned and it is not what the sentence cites.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'Lipid droplet' is a genuine ledger string, so any string-presence check succeeds; the validator does not verify that the claim type (function) matches the field type (localisation).
defects.suggested_fix: 'UniProt localises PNPLA3 to membrane and lipid droplet and annotates it as an acyltransferase; the dossier returns no pathway or functional-role statement.'

defects.quote: with no Mendelian randomization estimates or target-disease associations reported in Open Targets
defects.why_wrong: get_target_disease_evidence returned found=false with an explicit warning: 'OR51E2 is not among the top 500 associated targets for MONDO_0005027 (epilepsy). This is a TRUNCATED LOOKUP, not proof of no association.' The card restates a rank cut-off as 'no target-disease associations reported', which is a different and stronger statement — Open Targets may well hold an association below rank 500. The MR half is subject to the same tool warning ('ABSENCE OF AN ESTIMATE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF NO EFFECT') and the paragraph never carries either caveat forward.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: found=false plus a negative verdict looks maximally conservative to a checker built to catch overclaiming; there is no rule that a declared truncation must be surfaced, and no number or token is involved.
defects.suggested_fix: 'Open Targets did not return a score because OR51E2 falls outside the top 500 targets ranked for epilepsy (MONDO_0005027) — a truncated lookup, not a demonstrated absence of association; EpiGraphDB holds no pQTL instrument for this protein, which is likewise not evidence of no effect.'

defects.quote: the absence of any functional or genetic link makes OR51E2 an unsuitable drug target for epilepsy based on current knowledge
defects.why_wrong: 'Absence of any genetic link' is contradicted by this card's own ledger: get_gwas_catalog returned found=true with 34 unique SNPs and 68 association rows at the OR51E2 locus (sweep_complete = true), and ClinVar returned 96 records. Those rows carry no trait labels, so they are not epilepsy evidence — but the correct statement is 'trait unknown', not 'none'. The bundle-wide asymmetry is the real defect: the same unlabelled GWAS rows are inflated into disease support on the HMGCR/PCSK9/PNPLA3 cards and erased into 'absence' here. 'Unsuitable drug target ... based on current knowledge' also converts three truncated or unavailable lookups into a global negative about the literature.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The checker verifies that stated claims are supported; it has no rule for ledger contents a card fails to mention, and a conservative verdict never trips an overclaim rule.
defects.suggested_fix: 'The GWAS sweep returns 68 association rows over 34 SNPs at this locus, but this endpoint returns no trait labels, so none can be attributed to epilepsy. No positive evidence for OR51E2 in epilepsy was retrieved; this run cannot establish the absence of such evidence.'

defects.quote: whose inhibition by coumarin anticoagulants is directly used for the prevention and treatment of venous thrombosis
defects.why_wrong: No tool in this card reports an indication, a treatment use or an outcome. ChEMBL returned 7 unnamed inhibitor entries by CHEMBL ID; PharmGKB returned drug names (warfarin, acenocoumarol, phenprocoumon, fluindione) attached to clinical annotations whose subject — as the card's own next sentence concedes — is 'dosing and toxicity outcomes'. The card converts a pharmacogenetic dose-response resource into proof of therapeutic indication for a specific disease. The therapeutic-use statement is the model's own knowledge, placed in the verdict line. The ledger even contains a counter-signal the card omits: UniProt lists VKORC1 disease entries 'Combined deficiency of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors 2' and 'Coumarin resistance', i.e. loss of function produces a bleeding phenotype.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: All four drug names are genuine ledger strings and the sentence avoids 'FDA-approved' and 'clinical trial'. The validator checks that named entities exist somewhere in the ledger, not that the RELATIONSHIP asserted between them (drug treats this disease via this target) was ever retrieved.
defects.suggested_fix: 'PharmGKB holds 38 VKORC1 clinical annotations (3 at level 1A, 5 at 1B, 8 at 2A) linking VKORC1 variation to coumarin dosing and toxicity; ChEMBL lists 7 inhibitor records against VKORC1. These establish a pharmacogenetic dose-response relationship, not an indication for venous thrombosis.'

defects.quote: the wealth of clinical and genetic validation leaves no doubt regarding the causal and therapeutic role of VKORC1 in thrombosis management
defects.why_wrong: get_target_disease_evidence returned genetic_association = 0.0312 for VKORC1 x HP_0004936 — effectively zero, the lowest genetic score in the entire bundle — alongside literature 0.2145. The overall 0.5856 the card quotes approvingly is carried almost entirely by the clinical datatype (0.9491), which in Open Targets reflects drug/pharmacological evidence, not evidence that VKORC1 variation causes thrombosis. Claiming 'genetic validation' therefore inverts the one number in the ledger that speaks to it, and 'causal role of VKORC1 in thrombosis' asserts disease aetiology where the evidence base is drug-response. get_mr_result returned found=false, so nothing causal was retrieved at all.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 0.5856 is quoted correctly and passes the numeric check; the contradicting datatype score is never quoted, so there is nothing for a value-matching checker to compare. The causal-language-without-MR rule fired on the HMGCR card for the word 'causal' but did not fire here, so the strongest unsupported claim in the card also slipped the one rule that covers it.
defects.suggested_fix: 'Open Targets scores this pair 0.5856 overall, driven by clinical evidence (0.9491); genetic association is 0.0312, i.e. essentially no genetic support for VKORC1 in venous thrombosis. No MR estimate is available. The case rests on pharmacology, not on causal genetics.'

defects.quote: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE — there is no direct genetic or causal evidence linking IL6R to Alzheimer's disease.
defects.why_wrong: get_target_disease_evidence returned genetic_association = 0.583 for IL6R x MONDO_0004975 (Alzheimer disease) — a substantial, disease-specific genetic-association score under exactly the ontology term requested. 'No direct genetic evidence' contradicts it. The reasoning further softens the score to 'general genetic data', a hedge with no basis in the return: the tool's own note states the scores describe MONDO_0004975 specifically. Under-reading evidence is as much a provenance failure as over-reading it, and here it drives the headline verdict.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The validator hunts for unsupported assertions, not for supported evidence that a card denies. A negative claim references nothing, so there is no token or number to check; the card was marked ok with 2 checks passed.
defects.suggested_fix: 'No MR estimate matched Alzheimer disease. Open Targets does report a moderate association (overall 0.3691; genetic_association 0.583, literature 0.4824) for IL6R x MONDO_0004975 — non-trivial genetic support, but no causal estimate for this outcome was retrieved.'

defects.quote: population constraint metrics show it is tolerant to loss-of-function (LOEUF 1.03), leaving its causal relevance to Alzheimer's disease unproven
defects.why_wrong: gnomAD constraint measures depletion of LoF variants in the general population; it is a target-safety metric and carries no information about any specific disease. The tool said so explicitly: 'LoF-tolerant: no population-level depletion of loss-of-function variants, which is reassuring but is NOT positive evidence of efficacy.' The card wires the constraint metric into the causal-relevance conclusion via 'Furthermore ... leaving its causal relevance to Alzheimer's disease unproven', making a disease-agnostic number look like it argues against this disease. The tool's caveat says the metric is not efficacy evidence in either direction; the card uses it as negative evidence.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: LOEUF 1.03 matches the ledger value 1.0306 within rounding, so the numeric check passes. The validator cannot see that a correctly-quoted number has been recruited to answer a question it does not address.
defects.suggested_fix: Separate the two: 'gnomAD shows IL6R is LoF-tolerant (LOEUF 1.03), which is reassuring for safety but is neither positive nor negative evidence on efficacy or disease relevance. The causal question is unresolved because no MR estimate matched this outcome.'

defects.quote: supported by clinical-stage antisense and RNAi inhibitors
defects.why_wrong: get_chembl_modulators returned two entries against target 'LPA mRNA' with actions 'RNAI INHIBITOR' and 'ANTISENSE INHIBITOR' and nothing else — no phase, no development status, no trial. 'Clinical-stage' (echoed in the reasoning as 'active clinical modulators') is the model recalling pelacarsen/olpasiran. It is directly contradicted by the one clinical number the run did retrieve: Open Targets clinical datatype score = 0.0061 for this target-disease pair, essentially nil clinical evidence. A development-stage claim also promotes druggability into disease evidence inside the verdict.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'clinical-stage' and 'active clinical modulators' evade the fixed 'clinical trial' token; both modalities are genuine ledger strings, so the substantive nouns check out and only the unretrieved status adjective is fabricated.
defects.suggested_fix: 'ChEMBL lists 2 modulators against LPA mRNA — one RNAi inhibitor, one antisense inhibitor — with no development-stage information returned. Open Targets clinical evidence for LPA x coronary artery disorder is 0.0061.'

defects.quote: GO — genetic and Mendelian randomization evidence supports a causal, protective role of IL6R inhibition in coronary heart disease.
defects.why_wrong: The retrieved estimate is beta = -0.0442 for the exposure 'IL6R protein level' on CHD. Read at face value, that says HIGHER genetically-proxied IL6R is associated with LOWER CHD risk — i.e. the protective direction is raising the protein, not inhibiting it. Nothing in the ledger bridges plasma protein level to drug direction (no mention of soluble vs membrane receptor, no direction-of-effect annotation, no drug-target Mendelian randomisation). The card silently converts a negative beta on protein abundance into an endorsement of an inhibitor. Compare the LPA card in the same bundle, where beta = +0.252 correctly yields 'elevated LPA increases risk, so inhibit'. Same tool, same outcome GWAS id 7, opposite sign, and here the sign is not honoured. In a portfolio meeting this is the difference between funding an antagonist and funding an agonist.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The number -0.044 is quoted correctly and matches the ledger numerically, so the fabricated-number check passes; an MR estimate exists so the causal-language check passes. The validator has no model of what the sign means or of which direction of modulation a negative beta endorses.
defects.suggested_fix: State the direction as retrieved: 'higher genetically-proxied circulating IL6R is associated with lower CHD risk (beta = -0.044)'. Then say explicitly that this run retrieved no evidence linking that exposure direction to receptor blockade, so the estimate does not by itself support an inhibitor. Downgrade to a directional-uncertainty flag rather than a GO on inhibition.

defects.quote: GO — Strong genetic and biological evidence supports TREM2 as a causal target for Alzheimer disease, through microglial activation and amyloid-beta clearance.
defects.why_wrong: 'through microglial activation and amyloid-beta clearance' appears nowhere in any of the eight tool returns. The UniProt dossier returns only protein_name ('Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2'), subcellular_location and a diseases list; there is no function field, no pathway field, no ligand field. The clause also smuggles in a therapeutic DIRECTION — 'activation' implies an agonist programme — which no tool in this run established. Worse, the one directional signal that IS in the ledger (UniProt lists 'Polycystic lipomembranous osteodysplasia with sclerosing leukoencephalopathy 2', a TREM2 loss-of-function syndrome) is never mentioned. The GO also rests on zero tractability: ChEMBL n_modulators = 0, PharmGKB found = false, and get_mr_result explicitly states TREM2 has pQTL estimates but none for Alzheimer disease. A GO with no causal estimate, no chemical matter and an invented mechanism is not defensible.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'microglial activation' and 'amyloid-beta clearance' are not on the fixed qualitative-claim list (monoclonal antibody, FDA-approved, small-molecule, clinical trial, gene therapy, pathogenic variant), contain no numbers, rsIDs or accessions, and the word 'causal' is separately tolerated here because the card's other sentence acknowledges no MR was retrieved.
defects.suggested_fix: Delete the mechanism clause. Restate the verdict as evidence-tier language the ledger supports: strong target-disease association (OT 0.5582, genetic_association 0.8622) with NO retrieved causal estimate for this indication and NO chemical matter in ChEMBL. If a direction is asserted, ground it in the ledger's own LoF syndrome annotation and say so.

defects.quote: reinforced by extensive GWAS catalog mappings (114 unique SNPs, including the well-known rs738409 variant)
defects.why_wrong: rs738409 is not in this run's ledger. get_gwas_catalog returned counts (114 unique SNPs, 256 rows) plus exactly six example rsIDs: rs4823182, rs11912828, rs2073080, rs8418, rs2179642, rs3788603. rs738409 is real biology (the I148M allele) and that is precisely why it is dangerous — no human reviewer will challenge it, yet the pipeline never retrieved it, so the mechanically-rendered PROVENANCE block cannot back it. The whole product promise is that every claim traces to the ledger; here a specific, checkable variant identifier was supplied from model memory and dressed as a retrieval. It also does the load-bearing work in the GO rationale, since PNPLA3's entire case is 'compelling human genetics'.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The fabricated-rsID check apparently only rejects rsIDs that fail a format or existence test, or only compares against rsIDs the card itself claims were returned; rs738409 is a well-formed, genuinely existing rsID, and the card hedges it as 'well-known' rather than as retrieved, so no literal string mismatch is triggered.
defects.suggested_fix: Either cite only rsIDs present in example_rsids, or add a ledger rule that any rsID in model-written text must appear verbatim in a tool return. If the specific causal variant matters, add a variant-level lookup tool call so rs738409 enters the ledger legitimately.

defects.quote: Although the gene shows extreme intolerance to loss-of-function variants in gnomAD, suggesting caution for inhibitory strategies, the overwhelming genetic and clinical validation establishes it as a prime target for epilepsy.
defects.why_wrong: pLI = 1.0 and LOEUF = 0.154 are the most extreme constraint values in the entire bundle, and the tool's own interpretation string says inhibiting this gene 'carries a safety warning'. The card acknowledges the warning and then overrides it with an Open Targets association score — but an association score is direction-agnostic: it says SCN2A variation relates to epilepsy, not that reducing SCN2A activity treats it. The ledger in fact points the other way: UniProt lists 'Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 11' and 'Episodic ataxia 9' for this gene, i.e. the ledger's own evidence is that perturbing SCN2A causes the neurological phenotype. Compounding it, the GO carries no tractability at all: ChEMBL returned n_modulators = 0 and matched 'SCN2A/SCN1B' (a heterodimer entity, CHEMBL4523672) rather than SCN2A, with the tool asking the caller to confirm the intended target. A GO on a maximally LoF-intolerant CNS ion channel with zero chemical matter and an unconfirmed target match would be rejected at portfolio review.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: Every number is real and correctly transcribed, and the card mentions the constraint result rather than hiding it — so no fabricated-value or omitted-caveat regex fires. The validator has no notion of a safety flag being rhetorically neutralised, nor that association scores carry no direction of modulation.
defects.suggested_fix: Do not let an association score answer a constraint warning. Split the verdict: strong disease-gene association, but the ledger supports no direction of modulation and flags severe on-target risk for inhibition (pLI 1.0, LOEUF 0.154, LoF-driven UniProt phenotypes) and zero tractability (ChEMBL 0 modulators, target matched to SCN2A/SCN1B). Correct call is CONDITIONAL / directional-biology-required, not GO.

defects.quote: Although gnomAD constraint metrics indicate loss-of-function intolerance and the EpiGraphDB pQTL resource has no available MR estimate, the extensive clinical legacy of HMGCR inhibition provides definitive proof of efficacy.
defects.why_wrong: Two distinct failures in one sentence. (1) A safety flag is answered with an efficacy argument. gnomAD returned pLI 0.9999 with the explicit interpretation 'inhibiting it carries a safety warning', and the ledger even contains the corroborating on-target phenotype — UniProt lists 'Muscular dystrophy, limb-girdle, autosomal recessive 28' for HMGCR — which the card never mentions. Efficacy legacy does not retire a myopathy liability; a target-validation reviewer needs that liability carried forward into the safety plan. (2) 'extensive clinical legacy' and 'definitive proof of efficacy' are not established by anything in this run. The strongest clinical items in the ledger are an Open Targets clinical datatype score (0.9984, which is itself drug-derived) and ten PharmGKB annotations that are all evidence level 3. Neither is proof of efficacy; both are model knowledge about statins doing the persuading.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The validator fired only on the token 'causal' in the verdict (checked: 0 claims). It has no rule for 'model acknowledges a declared caveat and then dismisses it', and 'definitive proof of efficacy' contains no number, accession or listed qualitative token.
defects.suggested_fix: Rewrite as: 'gnomAD flags HMGCR as LoF-intolerant (pLI 0.9999) and UniProt records a recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy at this locus — an on-target safety signal that must be carried into any inhibitor programme.' Replace 'definitive proof of efficacy' with what the ledger actually holds: Open Targets clinical datatype 0.9984 and PharmGKB level-3 annotations naming statins.

defects.quote: the wealth of clinical and genetic validation leaves no doubt regarding the causal and therapeutic role of VKORC1 in thrombosis management
defects.why_wrong: The ledger says the opposite about genetics. Open Targets returned genetic_association = 0.0312 for VKORC1 x HP_0004936 — effectively no genetic support — and literature = 0.2145. The card asserts 'genetic validation' and 'no doubt' on top of a score that is one of the weakest genetic signals in the whole bundle. Separately, get_mr_result returned found = false, so 'causal' is unsupported by exactly the rule the validator applied to the HMGCR card. For target validation this matters: the human-genetic case that VKORC1 modulation moves thrombosis risk was never made; what exists is that a drug happens to hit VKORC1.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The card never quotes the 0.0312 figure, so the numeric check has nothing to compare — the validator can catch invented numbers but not a qualitative claim that contradicts a number it never sees quoted. The causal-without-MR rule that fired on HMGCR did not fire here, apparently because the causal token is embedded in the noun phrase 'the causal and therapeutic role' rather than in a pattern the regex recognises.
defects.suggested_fix: State the split explicitly: 'Open Targets support is almost entirely the clinical datatype (0.9491); genetic association is 0.0312 and literature 0.2145. No pQTL MR estimate is available, so no causal claim is made in this run.' Drop 'leaves no doubt'.

defects.quote: is explicitly annotated in UniProt as playing a causal role in Alzheimer disease 17 via amyloid-beta and lipoprotein binding
defects.why_wrong: The word 'explicitly' makes this a provenance claim, and it is false. get_uniprot_dossier returned a diseases array containing the string 'Alzheimer disease 17' and nothing else on the subject — no causal-role statement, no binding partners, no amyloid-beta, no lipoprotein. A disease-association annotation is being upgraded to 'causal role', and two molecular interactions are attributed to a tool that returned no interaction data. This is the most reviewer-proof failure mode in the set: the sentence is broadly true of TREM2 biology, so a scientist reads past it, while the SOURCES block points at a UniProt record that does not say it.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'Alzheimer disease 17' is a verbatim ledger string, so any string-presence check passes. 'amyloid-beta' and 'lipoprotein binding' are not on the fixed qualitative-claim list and carry no numbers or accessions.
defects.suggested_fix: Reduce to what was returned: 'UniProt lists Alzheimer disease 17 and polycystic lipomembranous osteodysplasia with sclerosing leukoencephalopathy 2 among TREM2-associated diseases.' Remove 'explicitly', 'causal role', and both binding mechanisms, or add a function/interaction tool call that actually retrieves them.

defects.quote: PCSK9 has 246 GWAS associations and is successfully targeted therapeutically by RNAi and biologic modulators in clinical practice
defects.why_wrong: ChEMBL returned exactly two modulators, both 'RNAI INHIBITOR', against target CHEMBL4630662 whose name is 'PCSK9 mRNA'. There is no biologic, no antibody, and no development-stage or approval information anywhere in the ledger. 'biologic modulators' and 'in clinical practice' are imported from the model's knowledge of evolocumab and alirocumab. The target-resolution problem makes it worse: the text search resolved to the mRNA entity, not the secreted protein, so the lookup never visited the ChEMBL target where antibody modulators would be recorded — the card therefore asserts a modality class the query provably could not have seen. For a modality decision (siRNA vs mAb vs small molecule) this is the single most consequential line on the card.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The regex list covers 'monoclonal antibody' and 'FDA-approved'; 'biologic modulators' and 'in clinical practice' are paraphrases that evade both. The number 246 is genuine, which makes the sentence look checked.
defects.suggested_fix: Write: 'ChEMBL text search for PCSK9 resolved to the PCSK9 mRNA entity (CHEMBL4630662) and returned two RNAi inhibitors; no protein-level target was retrieved, so this run says nothing about antibody or small-molecule tractability, nor about approval status.'

defects.quote: population constraint metrics show it is tolerant to loss-of-function (LOEUF 1.03), leaving its causal relevance to Alzheimer's disease unproven
defects.why_wrong: The 'although X, ... leaving its causal relevance unproven' construction makes LoF tolerance part of the case AGAINST the target. Constraint metrics are a safety read-out about germline selection pressure; the tool's own interpretation string says LoF tolerance 'is reassuring but is NOT positive evidence of efficacy' — and by the same logic it is not evidence against causal relevance either. Here the only genuinely reassuring safety datum on the card has been recruited as a negative. On a real portfolio this reasoning would kill a tractable, well-characterised target for the wrong reason.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: LOEUF 1.03 matches the ledger value 1.0306 within rounding tolerance, and the card correctly labels the gene LoF-tolerant, so both the numeric and the interpretation-string checks pass. The validator cannot see that a safety metric has been placed in an efficacy argument.
defects.suggested_fix: Separate the two axes: 'LOEUF 1.03 indicates LoF tolerance — a favourable safety read for an inhibitor, but not evidence of efficacy in either direction.' Base the insufficiency verdict solely on the absence of a disease-matched MR estimate.

defects.quote: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE — there is no direct genetic or causal evidence linking IL6R to Alzheimer's disease.
defects.why_wrong: Open Targets returned genetic_association = 0.583 for IL6R against exactly MONDO_0004975 (Alzheimer disease) — a moderate, non-trivial genetic signal for the queried disease term. 'No direct genetic evidence' contradicts that, and the reasoning further softens it to 'general genetic data' when the score is disease-specific by construction. The correct statement is that no causal (MR) estimate matched this outcome, which is a different and much narrower claim. As written this is a NO-GO framing that discards a real genetic signal.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The card never quotes 0.583 (it quotes only the 0.3691 overall score, which is accurate), so there is no number to contradict. Negative existence claims of the form 'there is no X' are not covered by any of the validator's rules.
defects.suggested_fix: Rewrite as: 'No disease-matched pQTL MR estimate was retrieved for Alzheimer disease. Open Targets does report a genetic_association datatype score of 0.583 (overall 0.3691), so genetic evidence exists but no causal estimate is available in this resource.'

defects.quote: Retrieved published Mendelian randomization estimates suggest a significant protective effect of genetically proxied IL6R modulation on coronary heart disease (beta = -0.044, p = 2.2e-07).
defects.why_wrong: The MR tool attached an explicit instruction: 'Check cis_or_trans, steiger_direction_ok, and coloc_prob before treating this as causal; coloc_prob=null means colocalization was not available for this pair.' For this estimate steiger_direction_ok = 'NA', steiger_p = null, coloc_prob = null, ld_check = null, and n_snp = 1 (single-SNP Wald ratio on rs4129267). So two of the three checks the tool demanded are unavailable and the third is undone. The card reports only the cis-ness implicitly and asserts causality anyway. The contrast with the LPA card in the same bundle — steiger_direction_ok = TRUE, steiger_p = 0.0, ld_check = 1.0 — shows the pipeline can distinguish these; this card just does not.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: beta and p-value are transcribed correctly and an MR estimate exists, so both the numeric check and the causal-language-without-MR check pass. The validator does not inspect the quality fields inside the estimate object.
defects.suggested_fix: Require the reasoning to report the three quality fields whenever it uses an MR estimate: 'single-SNP cis Wald ratio (rs4129267); Steiger directionality not assessed (NA) and no colocalisation probability available, so directional and confounding assurance is incomplete.'

defects.quote: IL6R is well-druggable with known modulators and clinically approved receptor inhibitors (such as tocilizumab) already documented in PharmGKB
defects.why_wrong: PharmGKB returned three clinical annotations at evidence levels 3 and 4 (its two weakest tiers) and the drug name 'tocilizumab'. It returned no approval status, no indication and no regulatory data — PharmGKB documents gene-drug response associations, not marketing authorisation. 'Clinically approved' is model knowledge. It is also misleading in this specific context: Open Targets' clinical datatype score for IL6R against coronary artery disorder is 0.0061, i.e. essentially no clinical evidence for THIS indication, which the card omits while implying clinical validation.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The regex catches 'FDA-approved'; 'clinically approved' is a near-synonym outside the fixed list. The drug name tocilizumab genuinely appears in the ledger, which makes the surrounding sentence look sourced.
defects.suggested_fix: Write: 'PharmGKB records three clinical annotations (levels 3-4) for IL6R naming tocilizumab; ChEMBL lists four modulators (inhibitor/antagonist) with no modality or development stage returned. Open Targets clinical evidence for this indication is 0.0061.' Drop 'clinically approved'.

defects.quote: supported by clinical-stage antisense and RNAi inhibitors
defects.why_wrong: ChEMBL returned two entries against 'LPA mRNA': one 'RNAI INHIBITOR' and one 'ANTISENSE INHIBITOR'. The mechanisms are in the ledger; the development stage is not. ChEMBL_37 returned no phase, no trial, no status field for either compound. 'Clinical-stage' (repeated in the reasoning as 'active clinical modulators') is knowledge of pelacarsen and olpasiran, not a retrieval. This is a competitive-landscape claim: it tells a portfolio committee that the target is de-risked and that someone is ahead of us, which is exactly the kind of assertion that must be sourced. Open Targets' own clinical datatype score for LPA x coronary artery disorder is 0.0061, so the ledger arguably points the other way.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The fixed list contains 'clinical trial'; 'clinical-stage' and 'active clinical modulators' are not string matches for it. The mechanism words 'antisense' and 'RNAi' are verbatim ledger content, which lends the phrase false credibility.
defects.suggested_fix: Say what was returned: 'ChEMBL lists two LPA-mRNA-directed agents, one RNAi inhibitor and one antisense inhibitor; no development stage or approval status was retrieved in this run.'

defects.quote: ChEMBL identifies active clinical modulators, specifically antisense and RNAi inhibitors targeting LPA mRNA, indicating high druggability
defects.why_wrong: The only ChEMBL target retrieved is CHEMBL4662965, 'LPA mRNA' — an oligonucleotide target, not apolipoprotein(a) itself. The ledger contains zero protein-directed modulators, and UniProt returned 'Not annotated.' for subcellular location, so there is no ligandability evidence for the protein at all. 'High druggability' therefore overstates a position that is really 'knockdown-only, hepatocyte-delivery-dependent modality'. That distinction determines whether a small-molecule discovery programme is even on the table.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: Every entity named (LPA mRNA, antisense, RNAi) is verbatim in the tool return, so nothing is fabricated; 'high druggability' is an unquantified judgement with no token on the qualitative list.
defects.suggested_fix: Replace with 'tractable only via mRNA knockdown in this run — ChEMBL resolved LPA to the LPA mRNA target and returned no protein-directed modulators, so protein-level ligandability is unestablished.'

defects.quote: the absence of any functional or genetic link makes OR51E2 an unsuitable drug target for epilepsy based on current knowledge
defects.why_wrong: Both absences the card leans on are explicitly disclaimed by the tools that produced them. get_target_disease_evidence returned found = false with the note 'OR51E2 is not among the top 500 associated targets for MONDO_0005027 (epilepsy). This is a TRUNCATED LOOKUP, not proof of no association.' get_mr_result returned 'ABSENCE OF AN ESTIMATE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF NO EFFECT.' The card converts a rank-500 cutoff and a coverage gap into a positive statement that no link exists, and then into a target-level kill decision. The headline verdict (INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE) is right; the closing sentence quietly upgrades it to NO-GO on grounds the ledger forbids.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: There are no numbers, rsIDs or listed qualitative tokens in the sentence, and no causal assertion — the causal-language rule only fires on positive causal claims. The validator has no rule for 'model contradicts a caveat string the tool returned'.
defects.suggested_fix: End with: 'This run retrieved no epilepsy-linked evidence for OR51E2, but the Open Targets lookup was truncated at the top 500 targets and the MR resource does not cover this protein, so this is absence of retrieval, not absence of association. Deprioritise pending a non-truncated query.'

defects.quote: Furthermore, ClinVar lists thousands of records for the gene, including numerous pathogenic variants.
defects.why_wrong: get_clinvar_variants returned total_records = 3108 and pathogenic_in_sample = 11 with sample_size = 30, plus the explicit warning: 'Pathogenic count is over the 30 record(s) retrieved, NOT over all 3108 ClinVar records for this gene; it is a sample, not a rate.' Placing 'thousands of records' and 'numerous pathogenic variants' in the same clause projects the 11/30 sample onto the full 3108 and invites the reader to infer hundreds or thousands of pathogenic variants. The card then calls this 'extensive clinical variant data' in the verdict, making the inflated read load-bearing for the GO.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: Both '3108' (as 'thousands') and the pathogenic claim map to genuine ledger values, and 'pathogenic variant' is on the qualitative list but passes because pathogenic_in_sample is greater than zero. The validator compares numbers, not the denominator they are implicitly scaled to.
defects.suggested_fix: Write: 'ClinVar holds 3108 records for SCN2A; in the 30-record sample retrieved here, 11 were classified pathogenic. This is a sample, not a rate, and no phenotype breakdown was retrieved.'

defects.quote: UniProt confirms its primary function in voltage-dependent sodium permeability in excitable membranes and its direct link to epileptic encephalopathy and seizure disorders.
defects.why_wrong: get_uniprot_dossier returned four things: gene_symbol, accession Q99250, protein_name 'Sodium channel protein type 2 subunit alpha', subcellular_location ['Cell membrane'], and a diseases list. There is no function field in this tool's output. The phrase 'voltage-dependent sodium permeability in excitable membranes' is recalled UniProt prose, not retrieved content, and 'confirms' asserts that the tool said it. The disease half of the sentence is supportable from the diseases array; the function half is not.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'Sodium channel', 'epileptic encephalopathy' and 'seizures' echo real ledger strings closely enough that no fabricated-entity check trips, and function-text leakage is not one of the validator's categories.
defects.suggested_fix: Trim to what the dossier returned: 'UniProt records SCN2A as sodium channel protein type 2 subunit alpha (Q99250), cell-membrane localised, with associated diseases: benign familial infantile seizures 3, developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 11, and episodic ataxia 9.'

defects.quote: ClinVar records contain established pathogenic variants in TREM2 linked to neurodegenerative phenotypes
defects.why_wrong: get_clinvar_variants returns counts only: total_records 202, pathogenic_in_sample 5, sample_size 30. It carries no phenotype, condition or trait field whatsoever, so 'linked to neurodegenerative phenotypes' cannot come from it — that link is supplied by the model. 'Established' also inflates 5 hits in a 30-record sample, and the tool's sample-not-a-rate caveat is ignored. In an AD target dossier this sentence reads as human genetic validation of the disease link, which is precisely what it is not.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'pathogenic variant' is on the qualitative list but passes because pathogenic_in_sample is greater than zero; the phenotype attribution adds no number or entity for the regex to test.
defects.suggested_fix: Write: 'ClinVar holds 202 TREM2 records; 5 of the 30 sampled were pathogenic. The tool returns no phenotype annotation, so no disease linkage can be drawn from this call.'

defects.quote: The target-disease evidence shows strong clinical support (Open Targets score 0.5856, driven heavily by clinical evidence), and ChEMBL confirms multiple known modulators that act as inhibitors against VKORC1.
defects.why_wrong: The card presents three lines of support — Open Targets clinical 0.9491, ChEMBL's seven inhibitors, PharmGKB's 38 coumarin annotations — as if they corroborated one another. They are one fact counted three times: warfarin exists and hits VKORC1. Open Targets' clinical datatype is derived from known-drug/indication data, so it is downstream of the same ChEMBL fact the next clause cites. Strip the drug out and the ledger retains genetic_association 0.0312, literature 0.2145, and no MR estimate. For target validation this is the classic trap of confusing 'target of an existing drug used in the indication' with 'genetically validated causal target' — the former justifies no new programme.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 0.5856 is transcribed exactly and every cited source genuinely returned data. The validator checks whether claims trace to the ledger, not whether several claims trace to the same underlying fact.
defects.suggested_fix: Add an independence statement: 'Open Targets clinical evidence, ChEMBL modulators and PharmGKB annotations here all derive from coumarin pharmacology and are not independent. Independent genetic support for VKORC1 in venous thrombosis is essentially absent (genetic_association 0.0312).'

defects.quote: GO — VKORC1 is a well-established, clinically validated target whose inhibition by coumarin anticoagulants is directly used for the prevention and treatment of venous thrombosis.
defects.why_wrong: Two unsourced elements. (1) The indication claim: PharmGKB returned drug names and annotation evidence levels only — it records genotype-guided dosing and toxicity associations, not what a drug is indicated for. Nothing in this run states that coumarins are used to prevent or treat venous thrombosis; that is model knowledge. (2) The safety picture is inverted by omission: UniProt in this very ledger lists 'Combined deficiency of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors 2' for VKORC1 — the on-target bleeding phenotype of loss of VKORC1 function — and the card issues a GO on inhibition without mentioning it. The dose-limiting toxicity of this mechanism is sitting in the ledger, unread.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: warfarin and acenocoumarol are both genuine ledger strings from PharmGKB's drugs array, so the drug names check out; the indication is asserted in prose with no number, accession or listed token, and omissions are invisible to a regex.
defects.suggested_fix: Rewrite as: 'VKORC1 is the target of coumarin anticoagulants; PharmGKB holds 38 annotations (3 at level 1A) linking VKORC1 genotype to coumarin dosing and toxicity. Indication data were not retrieved in this run. UniProt records combined deficiency of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors 2 at this locus — the expected on-target bleeding liability of inhibition.'

defects.quote: While ChEMBL currently lists no small-molecule modulators, the compelling human genetics provide a strong GO rationale for target validation and drug discovery.
defects.why_wrong: get_chembl_modulators returned found = false with the note 'No ChEMBL target for PNPLA3.' The target lookup itself failed — there is no target record, therefore no modulator count of any kind was ever produced. The card reports this as ChEMBL listing zero modulators, and narrows it to 'small-molecule', which implies the query established that biologics or oligonucleotides might exist. Both readings are wrong and they point a discovery team in opposite directions: 'no chemical matter found' versus 'this target is not represented in ChEMBL, so tractability is unassessed'. The verdict repeats it as 'direct pharmacological modulators are currently absent from ChEMBL'.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: It flagged the token 'small-molecule' (its one hit on this card) but has no rule distinguishing found = false meaning 'entity not present' from a successful call returning an empty modulator list.
defects.suggested_fix: Write: 'ChEMBL text search returned no target record for PNPLA3, so tractability was not assessed in this run — this is an unresolved lookup, not a demonstration that no modulators exist.'

defects.quote: strong pharmacogenomic annotations with statins in PharmGKB
defects.why_wrong: PharmGKB returned n_clinical_annotations = 10 with evidence_level_counts = {'3': 10} — every single annotation is at level 3, the tier PharmGKB defines as low/preliminary. 'Strong' misreads the one field in that return that grades strength. The bundle contains the control: VKORC1 returns 3 annotations at 1A and 5 at 1B, which is what strong looks like. Separately, pharmacogenomic annotations describe inter-individual drug-response variability, not target-disease validation, so they should not sit in a sentence about the strength of the HMGCR-hypercholesterolemia association at all.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: No number is quoted, so there is nothing to compare against evidence_level_counts; 'strong' is an unquantified adjective outside the fixed token list.
defects.suggested_fix: Write: 'PharmGKB records 10 clinical annotations for HMGCR, all at evidence level 3 (preliminary), naming statins — these describe drug-response variability, not target validation.'

defects.quote: reinforced by numerous GWAS Catalog associations
defects.why_wrong: get_gwas_catalog returns gene-level counts with no trait field at all: 92 unique SNPs, 177 association rows, six example rsIDs, and nothing about which phenotypes those rows belong to. Placed immediately after the hypercholesterolemia association score and joined by 'reinforced by', the sentence tells the reader that 177 lipid associations corroborate the disease link, when the ledger cannot say whether a single one of them concerns cholesterol. The same tool returns 68 rows for OR51E2 and 140 for TREM2, so raw counts carry no target-specific signal. This pattern recurs across the bundle (PCSK9's '246 GWAS associations', TREM2's 'numerous associated SNPs').
defects.why_validator_missed_it: No count is quoted here, and where counts are quoted elsewhere they match the ledger exactly — the validator verifies the number, not the trait attribution, because the tool return has no trait field to compare against.
