defects.suggested_fix: Either add trait filtering to get_gwas_catalog so associations can be attributed to the queried disease, or constrain the reasoning to 'the GWAS Catalog reports 177 association rows across all traits for this gene; trait breakdown was not retrieved, so these do not speak to hypercholesterolemia specifically.'

defects.quote: ChEMBL lists multiple small-molecule inhibitors targeting this enzyme.
defects.why_wrong: get_chembl_modulators returned six drug entries as bare ChEMBL IDs with action 'INHIBITOR' and moa 'HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor'. No modality field is present in the return — nothing distinguishes small molecule from peptide, biologic or oligonucleotide. That statins are small molecules is true and is model knowledge. Low consequence here because it happens to be right, but it is the same generator behaviour that produced 'biologic modulators' on the PCSK9 card, where it is wrong and decision-relevant.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'small-molecule' is on the fixed qualitative list, but the validator stopped after firing the causal-claim rule on this card (checked: 0) and never evaluated it — it caught the identical token on the PNPLA3 and TREM2 cards.
defects.suggested_fix: Report modality only when a modality field exists: 'ChEMBL lists six inhibitors against CHEMBL402 (HMG-CoA reductase); modality is not specified in the returned records.' Also fix the validator so the qualitative-claim pass always runs, independent of earlier rule hits.

defects.quote: GO — genetic and Mendelian randomization evidence supports a causal, protective role of IL6R inhibition in coronary heart disease.
defects.why_wrong: The MR exposure in this row is the plasma IL6R protein level, and beta = -0.0441899892357374. Read from the ledger alone, that says genetically HIGHER IL6R protein is associated with LOWER CHD — which licenses 'raising IL6R is protective', i.e. the opposite of the card's claim that INHIBITION is protective. The sign reversal is only defensible via the Asp358Ala/rs2228145 shedding mechanism (the sIL6R-raising allele impairs classical IL-6 signalling), and that mechanism appears nowhere in this run's tool output. Proof the model is reading sign from memory rather than from the ledger: on the LPA card in the same bundle it applied the opposite convention correctly (beta = +0.2523 -> 'elevated LPA levels strongly increase coronary heart disease risk'), so a negative beta was silently flipped here to preserve a remembered conclusion. If a reviewer took the ledger at face value, this card would read as recommending the wrong direction of modulation.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: beta = -0.044 and p = 2.2e-07 are both quoted correctly and match the ledger numerically, so the numeric-tolerance check passes. The validator has no model of what the MR exposure is, and no rule mapping the sign of beta onto which direction of pharmacological modulation the estimate supports.
defects.suggested_fix: State the estimate in ledger terms: 'each SD higher genetically-predicted plasma IL6R was associated with lower CHD (beta -0.044, se 0.0085, p 2.2e-07, single cis instrument rs4129267)'. Then either drop the word 'inhibition' from the verdict, or add an explicit flag that translating this estimate into IL6R blockade requires the Asp358Ala receptor-shedding mechanism, which this run did not retrieve and which the pipeline therefore has not established.

defects.quote: through microglial activation and amyloid-beta clearance
defects.why_wrong: This is a mechanism-of-action claim placed in the verdict line itself. Nothing in this run's ledger mentions microglia, amyloid-beta, or clearance — I searched the whole bundle and those strings occur only in the model's own verdict and reasoning. get_uniprot_dossier returned protein_name 'Triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2', subcellular_location ['Cell membrane','Secreted','Secreted'], and a two-item disease-name list. No function annotation was returned at all. The sentence is correct biology and will therefore pass unchallenged by a reader, yet the pipeline never established one word of it — the exact failure mode the card format is supposed to prevent.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: It contains no number, no rsID, no accession, and none of the fixed qualitative tokens (monoclonal antibody, FDA-approved, small-molecule, clinical trial, gene therapy, pathogenic variant). A regex has nothing to bind to in a free-text mechanism claim.
defects.suggested_fix: Delete the mechanism clause from the verdict. If the card is to say anything about mechanism, it must come from a tool that returned it — this run's UniProt dossier does not include a function field, so the honest verdict stops at 'genetic association evidence; mechanism not retrieved in this run'.

defects.quote: is explicitly annotated in UniProt as playing a causal role in Alzheimer disease 17 via amyloid-beta and lipoprotein binding
defects.why_wrong: Two fabrications wrapped in a named-tool attribution, which is worse than an unattributed aside because it tells the reader the ledger can be checked. (1) get_uniprot_dossier returned the disease NAME 'Alzheimer disease 17' in a bare list; it returned no statement that TREM2 plays a 'causal role' — a UniProt disease-association entry is not a causal assertion. (2) 'via amyloid-beta and lipoprotein binding' is not in the returned object at all; the dossier has no binding, ligand, or function field. Attributing recalled UniProt prose to a call that did not return it makes the provenance block actively misleading.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The accession check confirms P-numbers and the disease string 'Alzheimer disease 17' does appear in the ledger, so the anchoring tokens are all real; the validator does not verify that the PREDICATE attached to a retrieved entity was also retrieved.
defects.suggested_fix: Reduce to what the tool returned: 'UniProt lists TREM2 under two disease entries: Polycystic lipomembranous osteodysplasia with sclerosing leukoencephalopathy 2, and Alzheimer disease 17.' Remove 'causal role' and the binding mechanism entirely.

defects.quote: reinforced by extensive GWAS catalog mappings (114 unique SNPs, including the well-known rs738409 variant)
defects.why_wrong: rs738409 is not in this run's ledger. I searched the entire bundle: the string '738409' occurs on exactly one line — this reasoning paragraph. get_gwas_catalog returned example_rsids = [rs4823182, rs11912828, rs2073080, rs8418, rs2179642, rs3788603]. The model supplied the famous I148M variant from pretrained memory and presented it as a retrieved mapping ('GWAS catalog mappings ... including'). This is the single worst instance in the bundle because the entire human-genetic case for PNPLA3 in MASLD rests on I148M — so the one variant that carries the argument is the one that was invented. A hepatology reviewer would nod at rs738409 and never check it.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The task states the validator catches fabricated rsIDs, and it ran on this card (checked: 7), yet reported only the 'small-molecule' qualitative claim. Either the rsID scan does not reach parenthetical text inside the reasoning body, or its membership test is being run against the wrong ledger slice. This should be treated as a validator bug, not merely a card defect — a fabricated rsID escaping a rule written specifically to catch fabricated rsIDs undermines confidence in the whole checker.
defects.suggested_fix: Remove 'including the well-known rs738409 variant'. Cite only rsIDs present in example_rsids, and note that get_gwas_catalog returns a gene-level sweep with no trait field, so the 114 SNPs are not shown to be MASLD associations. Separately, re-test the validator's rsID rule against this card as a regression case.

defects.quote: the wealth of clinical and genetic validation leaves no doubt regarding the causal and therapeutic role of VKORC1 in thrombosis management
defects.why_wrong: There is no genetic validation in this ledger — there is its opposite. get_target_disease_evidence returned genetic_association = 0.0312 (essentially zero) and literature = 0.2145; the 0.5856 overall is carried almost entirely by clinical = 0.9491. The card asserts 'wealth of ... genetic validation' over a near-null genetic score it never quotes. Worse, the clinical datatype in Open Targets is driven by known-drug evidence — i.e. the fact that coumarins target VKORC1 and are used in thrombosis. Using that score as evidence that VKORC1 is CAUSAL for thrombosis is circular: the drug indication is the input to the score, not an independent confirmation of it. And the direction is inverted against the ledger's own biology: get_uniprot_dossier returns 'Combined deficiency of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors 2' and 'Coumarin resistance', i.e. VKORC1 loss of function causes BLEEDING, not thrombosis. VKORC1 is a therapeutic handle, not a disease-causal gene, and the card conflates the two.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 0.0312 is never quoted, so there is no number for the numeric check to compare; 'genetic validation' is a bare qualitative phrase on no fixed list. The causal-claim-without-MR rule fired on the HMGCR card for the same pattern (get_mr_result found=false plus the word 'causal') but returned ok:true here — the rule is firing inconsistently, possibly because it scans only for 'causal' in certain positions or is suppressed by the preceding 'Although no pQTL-based Mendelian randomization estimate is available' hedge.
defects.suggested_fix: Rewrite as: 'Open Targets clinical evidence is high (0.9491) but genetic association is essentially null (0.0312); the clinical score is largely known-drug evidence and is therefore not independent of the fact that coumarins target VKORC1. No MR estimate is available. This card supports VKORC1 as a validated drug target for anticoagulation, not as a causal gene for venous thrombosis.' Drop 'causal' and 'no doubt'.

defects.quote: is successfully targeted therapeutically by RNAi and biologic modulators in clinical practice
defects.why_wrong: get_chembl_modulators resolved to target 'PCSK9 mRNA' (CHEMBL4630662) and returned exactly two entries, BOTH with action 'RNAI INHIBITOR'. There is no biologic, no antibody, and no approval or clinical-use status anywhere in this run's output. 'Biologic modulators' and 'in clinical practice' are recalled facts about evolocumab/alirocumab. This is also internally revealing: the ChEMBL note warns 'resolved to PCSK9 mRNA — confirm this is the intended target', i.e. the tool found the mRNA-directed target record and NOT the protein target record; the model papered over that gap with remembered antibody knowledge instead of flagging it.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'monoclonal antibody' and 'FDA-approved' are on the fixed qualitative list; 'biologic' and 'in clinical practice' are semantic synonyms that a literal token list cannot reach. The two RNAi entries also make the sentence look partly grounded, which is exactly why a substring check passes it.
defects.suggested_fix: 'ChEMBL (target resolved to PCSK9 mRNA, not the protein) lists two RNAi inhibitors. No protein-directed modulators and no approval or clinical-use status were retrieved in this run.' Add 'biologic', 'antibody', 'in clinical practice', 'clinically approved', 'clinical-stage' to the validator's qualitative-claim list.

defects.quote: Retrieved published Mendelian randomization estimates suggest a significant protective effect of genetically proxied IL6R modulation on coronary heart disease (beta = -0.044, p = 2.2e-07).
defects.why_wrong: This is the weakest MR row in the bundle presented as the strongest. The row is n_snp = 1, method 'Wald ratio', steiger_direction_ok = 'NA', steiger_p = null, coloc_prob = null, heterogeneity_q_p = null, ld_check = null. Every sensitivity analysis that would license the word 'causal' is either impossible (with one instrument there is no MR-Egger, no weighted median, no Cochran's Q) or explicitly unavailable. Reverse causation is not excluded (Steiger NA). LD confounding with a neighbouring gene's causal variant at 1q21 is not excluded (coloc_prob null, ld_check null). The tool's own note demanded exactly this: 'Check cis_or_trans ..., steiger_direction_ok, and coloc_prob before treating this as causal; coloc_prob=null means colocalization was not available for this pair.' The card checked none of the three and issued GO. Contrast the LPA row in the same bundle, which at least carries steiger_direction_ok TRUE and ld_check 1.0 — the card gives no hint that this estimate is materially weaker.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: -0.044 and 2.2e-07 match the ledger, and the card does not claim to have computed MR. The validator has no rule tying n_snp, coloc_prob, steiger_direction_ok or ld_check to the confidence adjectives the model is permitted to use.
defects.suggested_fix: Require the caveat block to be echoed in prose whenever any of {n_snp==1, coloc_prob==null, steiger_direction_ok in (NA,null)} holds: 'single-SNP Wald ratio on cis instrument rs4129267; no colocalization, no Steiger check, no heterogeneity test available — pleiotropy and LD confounding cannot be excluded.' A GO verdict should not be reachable from a row with three nulls and a Steiger of NA.

defects.quote: IL6R is well-druggable with known modulators and clinically approved receptor inhibitors (such as tocilizumab) already documented in PharmGKB
defects.why_wrong: get_pharmgkb_drug_gene returned the drug name 'tocilizumab' and 3 clinical annotations at evidence levels {3: 2, 4: 1} — the two LOWEST tiers on the PharmGKB scale. It returned nothing about regulatory approval; PharmGKB documents drug-response variation, not approval status. 'Clinically approved' is recalled knowledge presented as 'documented in PharmGKB'. Compounding this, the same card's Open Targets result gives clinical = 0.0061 for IL6R x coronary artery disorder — essentially no clinical evidence connecting IL6R modulation to CHD — and the card never mentions it while quoting the other two datatype scores from the same object.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'FDA-approved' is the listed token; 'clinically approved' evades it. The selective omission of clinical = 0.0061 is invisible to a checker that only verifies quoted numbers and never asks which numbers from a retrieved object were dropped.
defects.suggested_fix: 'PharmGKB lists tocilizumab with 3 annotations, all at evidence levels 3-4 (lowest tiers). Open Targets clinical evidence for this specific target-disease pair is 0.0061.' Remove the approval claim. Consider a validator rule that flags any card quoting a subset of datatype_scores while omitting one that contradicts the verdict.

defects.quote: UniProt confirms its primary function in voltage-dependent sodium permeability in excitable membranes
defects.why_wrong: get_uniprot_dossier for SCN2A returned exactly five content fields: gene_symbol, accession Q99250, protein_name 'Sodium channel protein type 2 subunit alpha', subcellular_location ['Cell membrane'], and a three-item disease list. There is no function field in this tool's return shape at all. The quoted phrase is UniProt's real function line reproduced from memory and attributed to a call that did not return it — I confirmed 'voltage' appears nowhere in any tool_results in this bundle. The word 'confirms' actively asserts that the ledger can be checked for this.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The accession and protein name are genuine, so all checkable tokens resolve; the validator does not verify that the CLAIMED SOURCE of a sentence actually returned that content, only that named entities exist somewhere in the ledger.
defects.suggested_fix: 'UniProt returns protein name Sodium channel protein type 2 subunit alpha, cell-membrane localization, and disease entries for benign familial infantile seizures 3, developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 11, and episodic ataxia 9. No function annotation was retrieved.' Add a validator rule: sentences of the form '<TOOL> confirms/shows/annotates X' must have X grounded in that specific tool's return object, not the union ledger.

defects.quote: Although the gene shows extreme intolerance to loss-of-function variants in gnomAD, suggesting caution for inhibitory strategies, the overwhelming genetic and clinical validation establishes it as a prime target for epilepsy.
defects.why_wrong: Everything in this ledger establishes that SCN2A VARIATION CAUSES epilepsy syndromes (Open Targets clinical 0.9986, genetic_association 0.9749; UniProt DEE11 and BFIS3; ClinVar 3108 records). None of it establishes that MODULATING SCN2A treats epilepsy, and none of it establishes in which direction. The two are different claims and the card fuses them. The constraint data is maximally hostile to the implied strategy: pLI = 1, LOEUF = 0.154, lof_z = 10.42, mis_z = 10.07, with the tool's own text reading 'inhibiting it carries a safety warning' — this is one of the most LoF-intolerant genes in the genome. get_chembl_modulators returned n_modulators = 0, which the card never mentions. A GO verdict that names a safety warning, rebuts it with association evidence that is logically orthogonal to it, offers no direction of modulation, and has zero tractable modulators does not follow from the assembled evidence.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The validator has no concept of 'disease gene is not the same as drug target', no direction-of-modulation model, and no rule requiring a tool-declared safety warning to survive into the verdict line rather than being absorbed into a subordinate 'Although' clause.
defects.suggested_fix: Downgrade to NO-GO or REVIEW for an inhibitory strategy: 'SCN2A is a validated epilepsy DISEASE gene, not a validated inhibitory target — gnomAD flags extreme LoF intolerance (pLI 1, LOEUF 0.154) and ChEMBL returns no modulators for the resolved target SCN2A/SCN1B. Direction of therapeutic modulation is not established by any tool in this run.' Add a rule blocking GO when get_gnomad_constraint returns LoF-INTOLERANT and no direction-of-effect evidence exists.

defects.quote: supported by clinical-stage antisense and RNAi inhibitors
defects.why_wrong: get_chembl_modulators returned two entries against target 'LPA mRNA' (CHEMBL4662965) with action 'RNAI INHIBITOR' and 'ANTISENSE INHIBITOR'. ChEMBL returned no development phase, no trial, no status field of any kind. 'Clinical-stage' (verdict) and 'active clinical modulators' (reasoning) are recalled facts about pelacarsen and olpasiran. This claim is doing real work — it is the second half of the verdict and it is what converts a genetic finding into a tractability argument — so it is precisely the sentence a portfolio reviewer would act on, and it was never retrieved.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'clinical trial' is the listed token; 'clinical-stage' and 'active clinical modulators' are not that literal string. Two genuine ChEMBL IDs anchor the sentence, so it reads as grounded.
defects.suggested_fix: 'ChEMBL lists two nucleic-acid inhibitors against LPA mRNA (one RNAi, one antisense). Development stage was not retrieved.' Extend the qualitative-claim token list to cover clinical-stage / in the clinic / clinically approved / late-stage / Phase.

defects.quote: GO — Robust genetic and causal evidence demonstrates that elevated LPA levels strongly increase coronary heart disease risk
defects.why_wrong: The direction is right, but 'Robust' and 'demonstrates' are the strongest available words applied to n_snp = 1, method 'Wald ratio', instrument rs55730499, coloc_prob = null, heterogeneity_q_p = null. With a single instrument there is no pleiotropy sensitivity analysis and no heterogeneity test, and the tool's note explicitly says 'coloc_prob=null means colocalization was not available for this pair' and instructs the reader to check it before treating the estimate as causal. The card ignores that instruction silently. It also fails to bank the evidence it actually has: steiger_direction_ok = 'TRUE' and ld_check = 1.0 are genuine strengths present in this row and unmentioned, so the card is simultaneously overclaiming and underciting.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: beta 0.2523 and p 5.4e-39 are not even quoted, so there is nothing numeric to check; the validator has no rule linking n_snp or coloc_prob to the confidence adjectives permitted in the verdict.
defects.suggested_fix: 'MR (retrieved, not computed): single cis instrument rs55730499, Wald ratio, beta +0.252 (se 0.019, p 5.4e-39); Steiger direction TRUE and LD check passed, but colocalization unavailable and no heterogeneity or pleiotropy test is possible with one SNP.' Replace 'Robust ... demonstrates' with 'consistent with'.

defects.quote: the absence of any functional or genetic link makes OR51E2 an unsuitable drug target for epilepsy
defects.why_wrong: Three tools explicitly told the card not to say this and it said it anyway. (1) get_target_disease_evidence: 'OR51E2 is not among the top 500 associated targets for MONDO_0005027 (epilepsy). This is a TRUNCATED LOOKUP, not proof of no association.' (2) get_mr_result: 'ABSENCE OF AN ESTIMATE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF NO EFFECT.' (3) Most concretely, get_gwas_catalog returned n_unique_snps = 34 and n_association_rows = 68 with sweep_complete = true — so 'absence of any ... genetic link' is factually contradicted by this card's own ledger. The correct verdict (INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE) is then quietly upgraded to a different and unsupported claim, 'unsuitable drug target', which is a NO-GO dressed as a null result. Under this lens the asymmetry matters: a truncated top-500 lookup has essentially no power to exclude a weak association, and the card treats it as decisive.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The validator is built to catch over-claiming in the positive direction — fabricated support and unlicensed causal language. It has no mirror rule for over-claiming in the NEGATIVE direction, and no mechanism to map a tool's declared 'this is not proof of absence' caveat onto absolute phrasing in the reasoning.
defects.suggested_fix: 'No MR estimate and no Open Targets association were retrieved, but both lookups are explicitly non-exhaustive (truncated top-500; pQTL resource covers only proteins with usable plasma instruments). GWAS Catalog does return 34 SNPs / 68 rows at this gene, trait unspecified. Verdict: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE — this run cannot distinguish no association from not-looked-up.' Add a validator rule keyed to the strings 'TRUNCATED LOOKUP' and 'NOT EVIDENCE OF NO EFFECT' that flags absolute negatives.

defects.quote: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE — there is no direct genetic or causal evidence linking IL6R to Alzheimer's disease.
defects.why_wrong: get_target_disease_evidence resolved to the exact requested term (MONDO_0004975, Alzheimer disease) and returned genetic_association = 0.583. That IS direct, disease-specific genetic evidence, and 0.583 is not a trace value. The reasoning then mischaracterises it as 'literature and general genetic data' — but the Open Targets genetic_association datatype is by construction specific to the resolved term, as the tool's own note states ('Scores below describe THAT term'). Calling a 0.583 term-specific genetic association 'general genetic data' and then asserting 'no direct genetic evidence' is a false negative on the strongest evidence the card retrieved. The absence of an MR estimate justifies 'no causal estimate available'; it does not justify erasing the genetic association.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The card quotes 0.3691 correctly, so the numeric check passes on the one number present. The un-quoted 0.583 — the number the verdict contradicts — is invisible to a rule that only verifies numbers the model chose to write down. The validator also has no false-negative detection at all.
defects.suggested_fix: 'Open Targets returns overall 0.3691 with genetic_association 0.583 and literature 0.4824 for MONDO_0004975. No pQTL MR estimate matched this outcome (IL6R has 133 outcomes in the resource, none of them Alzheimer disease). Verdict: INSUFFICIENT CAUSAL EVIDENCE — moderate genetic association exists but no causal estimate is available for this indication.'

defects.quote: the extensive clinical legacy of HMGCR inhibition provides definitive proof of efficacy
defects.why_wrong: No tool in this run returned a trial, an outcome, an approval, or an efficacy result. ChEMBL returned drug IDs and MOA strings; PharmGKB returned annotation counts and drug names; Open Targets returned a clinical datatype SCORE (0.9984), which is a weighted evidence aggregate and not a demonstration of efficacy. 'Extensive clinical legacy' and 'definitive proof of efficacy' are the 4S/CTT trial literature recalled from pretraining. This is the load-bearing sentence of the card — it is what overrides both the missing MR estimate and the gnomAD safety warning — and it is the one sentence with no provenance whatsoever.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: It contains no number, no identifier, and none of the fixed tokens. 'Definitive proof of efficacy' is a maximally strong claim expressed entirely in words the regex does not know about — and because it is TRUE of the biology, no human reviewer challenges it either.
defects.suggested_fix: 'Open Targets clinical datatype score is 0.9984 for this pair; ChEMBL lists 10 inhibitors. No trial result, approval status or efficacy outcome was retrieved by any tool in this run.' Remove 'definitive proof of efficacy' — a card must not use unretrieved knowledge to override retrieved warnings.

defects.quote: strong pharmacogenomic annotations with statins in PharmGKB
defects.why_wrong: get_pharmgkb_drug_gene returned n_clinical_annotations = 10 with evidence_level_counts = {'3': 10}. Every single annotation is at PharmGKB level 3 — the low-confidence tier (typically a single unreplicated study). 'Strong' inverts the scale. The contrast is available inside this same bundle: VKORC1 returns {'1A': 3, '1B': 5, '2A': 8, '3': 21, '4': 1}, i.e. genuinely high-tier annotations. A reviewer comparing the two cards would conclude HMGCR's pharmacogenomic support is comparable to VKORC1's when it is categorically weaker. Separately, PharmGKB annotations describe inter-individual DRUG-RESPONSE variation (dose, myopathy risk); they are not evidence that the target is efficacious, so they should not be cited in support of the efficacy conclusion at all.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: No number is quoted, so there is nothing to compare numerically. The validator does not know that PharmGKB evidence levels are an ordinal scale where 1A is strongest and 3-4 are weakest, so it cannot detect that an adjective has been attached in the wrong direction.
defects.suggested_fix: 'PharmGKB returns 10 clinical annotations, all at evidence level 3 (lowest tier), for statins.' Add a validator rule that maps evidence_level_counts onto permitted adjectives and rejects 'strong/extensive/robust' when the distribution is concentrated at levels 3-4.

defects.quote: Although gnomAD constraint metrics indicate loss-of-function intolerance and the EpiGraphDB pQTL resource has no available MR estimate,
defects.why_wrong: get_gnomad_constraint returned pLI = 0.99993, lof_z = 5.73, mis_z = 5.01, with the tool's own interpretation reading 'LoF-INTOLERANT ... so inhibiting it carries a safety warning.' The card demotes an explicit safety warning to a subordinate 'Although' clause and then rebuts it with an EFFICACY premise ('definitive proof of efficacy') — a non sequitur, since efficacy evidence cannot answer a safety flag. The warning then vanishes entirely from the verdict line, which reads 'GO — HMGCR is a strongly validated causal target ... backed by extensive genetic associations, clinical validation, and targeted inhibitors (statins)' with no caveat at all. Anyone reading only the verdict receives none of the safety signal the pipeline retrieved.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The caveat block is rendered mechanically elsewhere on the card, so the validator sees the warning as present in the artifact. It has no rule requiring that a tool-declared warning be reflected — rather than rhetorically dismissed — in the model-written verdict and reasoning.
defects.suggested_fix: Carry the flag into the verdict: 'GO with safety caveat — gnomAD flags HMGCR as LoF-intolerant (pLI 0.9999).' Add a validator rule: when get_gnomad_constraint returns LoF-INTOLERANT, the verdict line itself must contain a safety qualifier, and an 'Although <warning>, <efficacy claim>' construction should be rejected as a category mismatch.

defects.quote: GO — PCSK9 is a strongly validated causal target for high cholesterol, backed by robust genetic association, causal Mendelian randomization evidence, and existing therapeutics.
defects.why_wrong: The MR support is one row: n_snp = 1, method 'Wald ratio', instrument rs191448950, coloc_prob = null, heterogeneity_q_p = null. Colocalization is unavailable, so LD confounding is not excluded, and no pleiotropy or heterogeneity test is possible — the tool note asks for exactly this check and the card does not perform it. Additionally the outcome is 'Non-cancer illness code self-reported: high cholesterol' (UKB-a:108), a self-reported diagnosis/treatment phenotype, not a measured lipid level; it is contaminated by statin prescribing and by ascertainment, which is a materially weaker outcome than the HP_0003124 Hypercholesterolemia term the Open Targets half of the card is keyed to. The reasoning does disclose 'self-reported', which is good, but the verdict discards that qualifier and compresses the whole thing into 'causal Mendelian randomization evidence' for a 'strongly validated causal target'.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The card quotes no MR numbers at all, and the honest 'self-reported' disclosure in the reasoning is likely what let the causal-claim rule pass (checked: 1). The validator does not compare the MR outcome phenotype against the Open Targets resolved disease term, and has no n_snp/coloc rule.
defects.suggested_fix: Preserve the phenotype qualifier in the verdict and state the instrument limits: 'MR evidence is a single-SNP Wald ratio (rs191448950) against a SELF-REPORTED UK Biobank high-cholesterol code, not a measured LDL phenotype; colocalization unavailable. Note this differs from the HP_0003124 term used for the Open Targets score.'

defects.quote: PCSK9 has 246 GWAS associations
defects.why_wrong: Two problems the numeric check cannot see. (1) 246 is n_association_rows, i.e. SNP x study x trait RECORDS, over n_unique_snps = 107 — so it is not 246 independent associations, and quoting the larger figure inflates apparent evidence roughly 2.3-fold. (2) get_gwas_catalog carries NO trait field: it is a gene-level sweep across every trait in the catalog. Nothing in it establishes that any of these rows concern cholesterol. Placed mid-sentence between the hypercholesterolemia score and 'targeted therapeutically', it reads unambiguously as 246 cholesterol associations. The same pattern recurs across the bundle — HMGCR ('reinforced by numerous GWAS Catalog associations'), PNPLA3 ('extensive GWAS catalog mappings (114 unique SNPs)'), TREM2 ('the GWAS catalog reports numerous associated SNPs') — so it is a systematic tool-semantics error, not a one-off.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 246 appears verbatim in the ledger, so the numeric comparison passes cleanly. The validator checks that a number EXISTS; it has no model of what the number counts or which trait it belongs to, and no rule preventing a trait-agnostic count from being cited inside a disease-specific argument.
defects.suggested_fix: 'GWAS Catalog returns 107 unique SNPs across 246 association rows at this gene, spanning all traits — the tool does not report which traits, so these rows are not shown to be cholesterol associations.' Add a validator rule forbidding get_gwas_catalog counts from appearing in a clause whose subject is the target disease.

defects.quote: GO — Strong genetic and biological evidence supports TREM2 as a causal target for Alzheimer disease
defects.why_wrong: get_mr_result returned found = false with the note 'TREM2 HAS pQTL MR estimates in this resource, but NONE matched the requested disease Alzheimer disease. The other outcomes are listed for context only — do not present them as evidence about Alzheimer disease.' No causal estimate for this outcome exists in this run, so 'causal target' has no support. This is the identical pattern the validator DID flag on the HMGCR card as 'causal-claim-without-mr', yet here it returned ok: true with only 'small-molecule' flagged — so a scientist comparing the two cards receives contradictory signals about what the checker enforces.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: The rule appears to be suppressed when the reasoning body contains its own hedge — this card says 'no MR estimates specifically for Alzheimer disease were retrieved from pQTL resources', which may satisfy a proximity heuristic — while the unhedged 'causal target' claim sits in the VERDICT line, which the rule may not scan. Either way the rule is position-sensitive and inconsistent; it fired for HMGCR and not for TREM2 or VKORC1 on the same facts.
defects.suggested_fix: Replace with 'GO on genetic association — no causal estimate available'. Fix the validator rule to scan the verdict line independently of the reasoning body, and to treat a hedge elsewhere in the card as not licensing an unhedged causal claim in the verdict.

defects.quote: ClinVar records contain established pathogenic variants in TREM2 linked to neurodegenerative phenotypes
defects.why_wrong: Two errors. (1) get_clinvar_variants returned pathogenic_in_sample = 5 with sample_size = 30 out of total_records = 202, and the tool's note is explicit: 'Pathogenic count is over the 30 record(s) retrieved, NOT over all 202 ClinVar records for this gene; it is a sample, not a rate.' 'ClinVar records contain established pathogenic variants' with no denominator reads as a property of the 202, not of a 30-record sample. (2) More seriously, get_clinvar_variants returns NO phenotype for any variant — only counts. 'Linked to neurodegenerative phenotypes' is supplied entirely by the model, and inside a card arguing for Alzheimer disease it implies these 5 variants are AD variants. The only other neurological entry the ledger actually contains is UniProt's 'Polycystic lipomembranous osteodysplasia with sclerosing leukoencephalopathy 2' — a different condition — and nothing connects the 5 sampled ClinVar records to that or to AD.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'pathogenic variant' is on the fixed qualitative list and passes because pathogenic_in_sample = 5 > 0 — the rule checks existence, not whether the sampled count was extrapolated. The phenotype attribution has no checkable token at all.
defects.suggested_fix: 'ClinVar: 5 of 30 sampled records (of 202 total) are classified pathogenic; the tool returns no phenotype for these records, so their disease attribution is not established by this run.'

defects.quote: PharmGKB demonstrates extensive pharmacogenomic annotations linking VKORC1 variation to coumarin anticoagulants (such as warfarin and acenocoumarol) for dosing and toxicity outcomes
defects.why_wrong: get_pharmgkb_drug_gene returned only n_clinical_annotations (38), evidence_level_counts, a four-item drug-name list, a URL and a source release. It returned NO phenotype category — I confirmed 'dosing' and 'toxicity' appear nowhere in this bundle's tool output. Those are recalled facts about the CPIC warfarin guideline, attributed to a tool that returned counts only. The verdict compounds this with an indication claim — 'whose inhibition by coumarin anticoagulants is directly used for the prevention and treatment of venous thrombosis' — and no tool in this run returned a drug indication. ('Anticoagulants' as a pharmacological class is likewise not in the ledger; ChEMBL returns only 'Vitamin k epoxide reductase complex subunit 1 isoform 1 inhibitor'.) The irony is that the annotation counts here are the one genuinely strong pharmacogenomic signal in the bundle (3x 1A, 5x 1B, 8x 2A) and 'extensive' is fully earned — the model still could not resist decorating it with unretrieved specifics.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'Warfarin' and 'acenocoumarol' are real drug names in the ledger, so the anchoring entities all resolve; the validator does not check whether the PROPERTIES ascribed to a retrieved entity (annotation phenotype category, therapeutic indication, drug class) were themselves retrieved.
defects.suggested_fix: 'PharmGKB returns 38 clinical annotations for VKORC1 across acenocoumarol, fluindione, phenprocoumon and warfarin, including 3 at level 1A and 5 at level 1B (highest tiers). The annotation phenotype categories and the drugs indications were not retrieved.'

defects.quote: population constraint metrics show it is tolerant to loss-of-function (LOEUF 1.03), leaving its causal relevance to Alzheimer's disease unproven
defects.why_wrong: The 'Furthermore ... leaving unproven' construction makes gnomAD constraint a premise in a conclusion about disease causality. Constraint measures depletion of LoF variants under natural selection in a population sample; it is orthogonal to whether a protein lies on a causal path to a late-onset disease, and it cannot argue either for or against causal relevance. The tool itself states the boundary — 'reassuring but is NOT positive evidence of efficacy' — i.e. it is not evidence in either direction. The verdict happens to land in a defensible place, but the reasoning gets there partly through an invalid inferential step, which is the kind of thing that propagates into the next card.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: LOEUF 1.03 is quoted correctly (1.0306 in the ledger) and matches numerically. The validator checks whether a number is real, not whether the inference drawn from it is valid.
defects.suggested_fix: Split the clause: 'gnomAD shows LoF tolerance (LOEUF 1.03), which is reassuring for safety but is not evidence about efficacy or about causal relevance in either direction. Causal relevance remains unestablished because no MR estimate matched this outcome.'

defects.quote: ClinVar lists thousands of records for the gene, including numerous pathogenic variants
defects.why_wrong: total_records = 3108 supports 'thousands', but pathogenic_in_sample = 11 is over sample_size = 30, and the tool's note is explicit that this 'is a sample, not a rate'. Placing 'numerous pathogenic variants' immediately after 'thousands of records for the gene' invites the reader to scale 11/30 up to the 3108 — which would imply roughly 1,100 pathogenic records, a number the pipeline never established. The claim is defensible about the sample and misleading about the gene.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'pathogenic variant' is on the fixed qualitative list and passes because pathogenic_in_sample = 11 > 0; the rule tests existence, not whether a sampled numerator was implicitly rebased onto the full denominator.
defects.suggested_fix: 'ClinVar holds 3108 records for SCN2A; of the 30 sampled, 11 are classified pathogenic (a sample, not a rate).'

defects.quote: UniProt confirms its primary role in lipid droplet metabolism
defects.why_wrong: get_uniprot_dossier returned protein_name '1-acylglycerol-3-phosphate O-acyltransferase PNPLA3' and subcellular_location ['Membrane','Lipid droplet']. Subcellular LOCALIZATION to the lipid droplet is not the same as a functional ROLE in lipid droplet metabolism, still less a 'primary' one — plenty of proteins localize to organelles whose metabolism they do not drive. The tool returned no function field, so 'confirms' overstates what was retrieved. Mild compared with the SCN2A and TREM2 instances of the same pattern, but it is the same pattern.
defects.why_validator_missed_it: 'Lipid droplet' is a genuine string in the ledger, so the anchoring token resolves; the validator does not distinguish a localization annotation from a functional claim built on top of it.
defects.suggested_fix: 'UniProt localizes PNPLA3 to membrane and lipid droplet and names it an 1-acylglycerol-3-phosphate O-acyltransferase; no function annotation was retrieved.'

verdicts.reason: Verified against bundle_trim.json lines 165-308. The quote is exact (verdict line 166) and the ledger contradicts it. get_target_disease_evidence returned found=true, efo_id=MONDO_0004975, resolved_disease_name='Alzheimer disease' — the exact requested term — with datatype_scores.genetic_association = 0.583 and literature = 0.4824. The tool's own note states 'Scores below describe THAT term, not the free-text phrase', so 0.583 is by construction disease-specific genetic evidence. The verdict's flat 'there is no direct genetic or causal evidence linking IL6R to Alzheimer's disease' therefore denies the single strongest piece of evidence the run retrieved. I tested three defenses and all fail: (1) reading 'genetic' as shorthand for 'causal-genetic' makes the verdict's own 'or causal' clause redundant, and the reasoning distinguishes them explicitly ('no dedicated causal genetic support'); (2) 0.583 is not a trace value by this card's own calibration — the sibling IL6R x coronary heart disease card (line 312) calls genetic_association 0.92 'high' at a comparable overall score, and nothing in the ledger marks 0.583 as sub-threshold; (3) 'literature and general genetic data' is not a fair gloss — the tool pre-empted exactly that framing with its resolution note, and genetic_association (0.583) is in fact the LARGER datatype, so 'driven by literature' also inverts the ledger's contribution ordering. This is both a verdict-contradicts-ledger false negative and a quiet contradiction of a caveat the tool declared. The empty matched_disease_estimates (with n_outcomes_available=133) justifies only 'no causal estimate available'; the model correctly refrained from importing the other 133 outcomes, but that absence does not license erasing the genetic association. Named offending field: get_target_disease_evidence.datatype_scores.genetic_association = 0.583 under efo_id MONDO_0004975. Severity major rather than critical: no direction/sign error and no wrong-disease attribution, the GO/NO-GO call itself is survivable, and the mechanically rendered evidence table still exposes 0.583 to the reader — but the verdict line is the sentence most likely to be quoted in isolation, and it asserts the absence of evidence the pipeline actually retrieved.

Upheld. The quote is verbatim from the LPA card's verdict (line 474: "supported by clinical-stage antisense and RNAi inhibitors"), reinforced in the reasoning ("ChEMBL identifies active clinical modulators, specifically antisense and RNAi inhibitors targeting LPA mRNA"). The specific tool field that makes it unearned: get_chembl_modulators returned modulator objects containing exactly three keys each — drug, action, moa (CHEMBL4650413 / "RNAI INHIBITOR", CHEMBL4298202 / "ANTISENSE INHIBITOR"). There is no max_phase, development_phase, or status field. A case-insensitive grep for "phase" across all 1416 lines of the bundle hits ONLY model-written verdict/reasoning text and never appears inside any tool_results block for any of the 10 cards, confirming the pipeline never retrieved development stage at all. Alternative sources ruled out: Open Targets datatype_scores.clinical = 0.0061 (near-zero, would undercut not support, and the sentence attributes to ChEMBL); PharmGKB for LPA returns only "HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors" and "rosuvastatin" (statins, not the antisense/RNAi agents named). "Clinical-stage" is a term of art meaning the asset entered human trials — a recalled fact about pelacarsen/olpasiran. The same leakage recurs in the PCSK9 card ("in clinical practice") from an identically stage-free ChEMBL return, showing a systematic gap. Severity major rather than critical: the MR half of the verdict is sound (beta +0.252, cis instrument, steiger_direction_ok TRUE, ld_check 1.0, p=5.4e-39 — correct sign, correct disease), so there is no direction or wrong-disease error; but the unearned clause is the second half of a GO verdict and the sole basis for its tractability argument. Minor caveat on the auditor's own framing: the declared lens (statistical genetics / MR methodology) mislabels what is actually a ChEMBL provenance defect — a labeling flaw, not grounds to refute the substance.

UPHELD. The quote is verbatim from the card's reasoning: \"...the absence of any functional or genetic link makes OR51E2 an unsuitable drug target for epilepsy based on current knowledge.\" Three named ledger fields make it unearned. (1) get_target_disease_evidence.note states in capitals: \"OR51E2 is not among the top 500 associated targets for MONDO_0005027 (epilepsy). This is a TRUNCATED LOOKUP, not proof of no association.\" (2) get_mr_result.note states: \"ABSENCE OF AN ESTIMATE IS NOT EVIDENCE OF NO EFFECT.\" Both tools explicitly declare their nulls non-probative, and the reasoning converts them into an absolute \"absence of any ... link.\" (3) get_gwas_catalog returned found=true, n_unique_snps=34, n_association_rows=68, sweep_complete=true with six concrete rsIDs; the one genetic-association tool that did return data at this locus is not mentioned at all while the card asserts absence of any genetic link. The auditor slightly overstates point (3) — those rows are trait-unspecified and so do not establish an epilepsy link — but that cuts the same direction: the run never determined what the 68 rows are about, so it cannot assert absence either. The auditor's own suggested fix acknowledges this (\"trait unspecified\"), so the rationale is not fabricated. This is also an internal inconsistency, not a style quibble: the verdict field says \"INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE\" and its phrasing there (\"no genetic or experimental evidence directly linking OR51E2 to epilepsy\") is defensible, but the reasoning's closing sentence silently upgrades to a different decision class — \"unsuitable drug target,\" a NO-GO — and attributes it specifically to the false premise of absent linkage rather than to the genuinely supported facts (get_chembl_modulators.n_modulators=0, get_pharmgkb_drug_gene.found=false). The hedge \"based on current knowledge\" modifies the conclusion, not the premise. This is squarely the declared defect class \"caveats the tool declared that the reasoning then contradicts or quietly ignores.\" Validator recorded ok=true, checked=0, consistent with having no rule that fires on absolute negatives.

UPHELD. The quote is verbatim from line 312 of the IL6R x coronary heart disease reasoning: "Furthermore, IL6R is well-druggable with known modulators and clinically approved receptor inhibitors (such as tocilizumab) already documented in PharmGKB." The specific field that makes it unearned: get_pharmgkb_drug_gene for this card returns only gene_symbol, n_clinical_annotations (3), evidence_level_counts ({"3":2,"4":1}), drugs (["tocilizumab"]), n_drugs (1), url, source_release. There is no approval/phase/regulatory field. get_chembl_modulators likewise exposes only drug (CHEMBL ID), action, and moa per entry -- no max_phase. A grep for "approved" across the whole bundle returns exactly one hit: line 312, the model's own sentence. No tool anywhere in the run emitted approval status, so "clinically approved" is recalled knowledge, and "already documented in PharmGKB" misattributes it to a resource that documents drug-response variation at evidence levels 3-4 (the two lowest tiers), not licensure. I tested the defense that "clinically approved" merely paraphrases a PharmGKB clinical annotation; it fails, since even a level-1A annotation would not establish approval. The compounding point also holds: get_target_disease_evidence returned datatype_scores {literature 0.8678, genetic_association 0.92, clinical 0.0061} and the card quotes overall_score and genetic_association while dropping clinical = 0.0061 -- the one field bearing on clinical evidence for this exact pair -- immediately before asserting "clinically approved" inhibitors under a GO verdict. One correction to the auditor's wording: the card quotes overall_score plus genetic_association, not "the other two datatype scores" (literature 0.8678 was also omitted); this does not affect the substance. Severity major is correct: the sentence is true of the biology so no reviewer catches it, and the validator returned ok:true because "FDA-approved" is the listed token while "clinically approved" evades it.

Verified and upheld, with severity corrected downward. The quote is verbatim from the model-written reasoning of PNPLA3 x MASLD (bundle line 882) and is correctly attributed. A grep for "738409" across the entire bundle returns exactly one hit — that same reasoning line — confirming the identifier appears nowhere in any tool return. The text is real. Line 1007 of bundle_trim.json, in the "SCN2A x epilepsy" reasoning: "Furthermore, ClinVar lists thousands of records for the gene, including numerous pathogenic variants." So the auditor is not misattributing.

But both halves of that clause are directly earned by the ledger, and no tool field contradicts or exceeds either one:

- "thousands of records for the gene" -> get_clinvar_variants.total_records = 3108. The auditor concedes this.
- "including numerous pathogenic variants" -> get_clinvar_variants.pathogenic_in_sample = 11. Those 11 are genuine ClinVar records for SCN2A; the sample was drawn FROM the 3108. So it is literally, verifiably true that ClinVar's SCN2A holdings include at least 11 records classified pathogenic. "Numerous" is an existence-and-plurality claim about the pathogenic records themselves, and 11 discharges it.

The allegation fails the "name the specific tool field that makes the statement wrong" test. There is none. The auditor's own case makes this clear: he must supply the offending number himself ("which would imply roughly 1,100 pathogenic records") because the card never states it. The card gives no rate, no proportion, no percentage, no scaled count, and no "of these" construction. It does not say "many of the 3108 are pathogenic," nor "a high proportion," nor "11 in 30, therefore ~1,100." The 1,100 figure exists only in the audit, not in the artifact under review.

The tool's caveat is also not contradicted or ignored. The note forbids one specific act: presenting the sampled count AS A RATE over the full denominator ("it is a sample, not a rate"). The card states no rate, so there is nothing for the note to contradict. This is materially different from the genuine sampled-count-as-population defect pattern, where a card converts a sampled numerator into a population statement — the diagnostic signature of that defect is a stated or numerically implied proportion, and this sentence has neither.

What remains is an objection to clause adjacency — that putting "numerous pathogenic variants" after "thousands of records" may prompt a reader to extrapolate on his own. That is an implicature/emphasis preference about how a defensible true statement is arranged, not a defect in the statement. The auditor effectively admits this: "The claim is defensible about the sample." A claim that is defensible is not a defect. The suggested rewrite ("3108 records; of the 30 sampled, 11 are classified pathogenic") is more precise and would be a fine style edit, but the original is not wrong, not unearned, and not misleading about any number the pipeline actually established.

Two further checks against upholding this on a lesser theory: (1) The clause is not doing load-bearing work for the verdict — the GO rests on Open Targets overall_score 0.9057 with clinical 0.9986 and genetic_association 0.9749, plus the UniProt disease annotations (Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 11; Seizures, benign familial infantile, 3). Even striking the ClinVar sentence entirely leaves the verdict intact, so there is no downstream harm. (2) The card does not quietly ignore the gnomAD caveat either — it explicitly carries "extreme intolerance to loss-of-function variants in gnomAD, suggesting caution for inhibitory strategies," matching the tool's LoF-INTOLERANT interpretation (pLI 1, LOEUF 0.154). Nothing nearby aggravates the quoted clause.

Upholding this would penalize a true, traceable, non-quantified sentence for a reader inference it never invites in words, and would cost the owner time better spent on cards where a tool field is actually contradicted.
